Do not 'fix' validIdent to accept escaped colons without re-adding an explicit volatile-id blocklist.

`structuralSelector` has NO depth cap (it walks to documentElement) and NEVER verifies the final joined selector with querySelectorAll — every intermediate tier is verified, the fallback is not. Both need adding.

SHADOW-SCOPE BUG: `isUnique` hardcodes `document.querySelectorAll`, but `buildSelector` is called on shadow-DOM elements (content.js 6450). Uniqueness is measured in the wrong scope; the scanner then queries with `scopeOf(el).querySelectorAll(buildSelector(el))` at line 6455, mixing scopes. Thread an explicit scope through the whole selector path.
`buildXPath`'s id fast path does NOT verify uniqueness (unlike the CSS path, which does) and does NOT escape a `"` inside the id — a quoted id yields a syntactically broken XPath.

DEAD FIELD: `collect()` never sets `data.url`, but sidepanel.js reads `lastPick?.data?.url` twice (lines 696 and 1068) for the library `host` and the export `source.url`. Both are permanently undefined, so saved components lose their provenance. Add `url: location.href` to collect().

The accessible name is NOT the ARIA accname algorithm — roughly 30% of it, in the wrong order. Missing aria-labelledby (the spec's FIRST check after hidden-ness), <label for>, legend/caption/figcaption, input value, placeholder, ::before/::after content, and implicit role computation. It also reads `textContent`, which includes display:none and aria-hidden subtrees the spec excludes. In Electron, replace it wholesale with CDP `Accessibility.getPartialAXTree`.

KEY_STYLES is 24 properties, not 25. Its selection logic is: shorthands only where they exist (margin/padding/border/border-radius collapse ~24 longhands into 4), one property per layout DECISION rather than per layout system, and the full type ramp. It deliberately omits box-shadow, transform, transition, gradients and letter-spacing — those live in the 46-property INLINE_PROPS list used by the standalone-HTML export. It is also OFF by default because the Tailwind inference covers the same ground more compactly.

`toTailwind` emits NO margin, NO width, NO height and NO variants (hover:/focus:/md:), and collapses any box-shadow to the bare word `shadow`, discarding the value. `opacity-${round(op*100)}` is not snapped to Tailwind's step-5 scale, so it can emit `opacity-73`. Borders are read from `borderTop*` only and assumed uniform.

`twSpace` is the trick worth stealing: the whole Tailwind spacing scale is px/4 for multiples of 4 up to 384px, so `n % 4 === 0 && n/4 <= 96 ? String(n/4) : '['+n+'px]'` needs no dictionary and degrades gracefully to arbitrary values.

The readable-mode class truncation writes a literal `…` INTO the class attribute (`class="a b c … "`) when there are more than 8 classes. The result looks pasteable and is functionally dead — that is exactly why `verbatim` mode exists, per the comment at content.js 495–502. Use a comment node instead in the port.

TOKEN BUDGET (IDEAS.md #4) DID NOT SHIP. Verified by exhaustive grep: no token counter, no estimateTokens, no budget switch, no degradation ladder, no dropped-fields report anywhere on the element path. The real AI hand-off is sidepanel.js ~3512: `(d.outerHTML || '').slice(0, 1500)` with `maxTokens: 1000`, and it discards the xpath, attributes, accessibility, tailwind, metrics and computed styles that collect() just built. The only budgeted exporter that shipped is `getCodeForReview(budget=60000)` — a BYTE budget over source code.

REDACTION CHOKE POINT (IDEAS.md #16) DID NOT SHIP. `scrubPII` exists but is wired only to the Arabic-corpus harvester (call sites 7061/7107/7165), and it REMOVES rather than substitutes — the opposite of the length-preserving policy the idea specifies. `PII_RULES`/`maskMatch` are the security scanner's report renderer with masking OPT-IN and defaulting to FALSE. Element picks reach the LLM completely unredacted. Treat this as a launch blocker for deliverable (c), not a follow-up.

ARABIC-INDIC DIGIT TRAP (directly applicable to EXELMJ's Arabic-first brief): `\b` is ASCII-only and never fires next to `٠-٩`, so an ASCII digit-run regex silently skips every Arabic-Indic number. scrubPII carries a SECOND rule `[٠-٩][٠-٩\s.-]{5,}[٠-٩]` specifically for this. Any regex-based redaction in EXELMJ must be duplicated for the Arabic-Indic range.

MASKING DESIGN LESSON worth carrying verbatim (content.js 3491–3497): mask by WHAT the data is (`ALWAYS_MASK` set of 17 rule ids), never by how severe it was judged — tying masking to severity meant reclassifying a token as low-risk silently printed it in full into a report the user pastes into a chat.

`inert(s)` in componentBundle (`.replace(/<\/(script|style)/gi,'<\\/$1').replace(/<!--/g,'<\\!--')`) is applied to the WHOLE handler body including event names, because those come from the page. Any EXELMJ code path that embeds captured page content into generated markup needs the same guard.

MEASURED NUMBERS from the source and Session-Notes: deepAll caps at 9000 nodes / depth 14; extractStyles caps at 5000 elements; getCodeForReview takes at most 12 external files, 8s AbortController timeout, 400KB per file, skips minified files >20KB; isMinified = longest line >500 chars, or <5 lines and >2000 chars; the component library hits a hard 10MB chrome.storage.local ceiling and warns at 8MB; `libId` had to add text length + first 40 chars after 144 same-sized cards from one page collided on six fields; 12 of 94 keyframes in one motion library referenced a var(), which is why ancestorContext has a keyframes second pass; the component scanner went 7→144 cards on one site after the dedup-signature fix while MDN as a control grew 0.8%.

`chrome.dom.openOrClosedShadowRoot` is the ONLY genuinely extension-exclusive API in this subsystem, and its CDP replacement (`DOM.getDocument({pierce:true})`) is strictly better — it returns shadowRootType per node. The port LOSES nothing here and gains cross-origin iframes and cross-origin stylesheets, both of which the extension explicitly gave up on.

codeBlocksIn reads code out of `display:none` tab panels via textContent — no clicking, no page mutation, so hidden tabs' contents come for free. Its label fallback order deliberately puts the block's own language above `closest('[id]')?.id`, because closest walks to the page section and would label every snippet on the page identically.

subsystem: Component Extraction and Environment Reconstruction (content.js CSS-excavation + rule-index + ancestor-context + componentCss; sidepanel.js componentBundle + previewDoc)
summary: This is the engine that turns "that card on that website" into a paste-able artifact that still renders and still animates. It does NOT read computed styles as its primary source: it walks the already-parsed CSSOM per tree scope, indexes every style rule once, splits the index into "resting" and "state" halves, then asks for each rule "does the element this rule paints live inside my subtree?" and ships the author's own declarations verbatim. Around that it reconstructs the five things a snipped element loses — inherited text properties, custom-property values (lifted from authored `var()` references, not from resolved computed values), theme classes on ancestors, the parent's flex/grid mode, and the backdrop colour — plus @property registrations, scroll/view-timeline declarations that live on ancestors, and every @keyframes any state can reach. The final artifact is a single string: HTML comment header, a `<style>` block, the verbatim markup, and an inert `<script type="text/plain">` reference block holding the page's real handlers. Every page-controlled string that lands in that artifact is passed through a 2-rule escaper so it cannot close the block it lives in.

mechanisms.name: Per-tree-scope rule index (the whole extractor's spine)
mechanisms.problem: Walking every stylesheet once per component is O(components x rules) and stalls a real site (a Tailwind sheet is ~20k rules, a gallery has 600 components). Worse: a stylesheet inside a shadow root applies only inside it, and document rules never cross the boundary, so indexing only `document` returns ZERO CSS for component showcases (uiverse.io and its clones give every item its own shadow root with its own <style>) — those components used to come back unstyled and stateless.
mechanisms.how_it_works: `_ruleIndex` is a WeakMap keyed by TREE SCOPE, not by document. `scopeOf(node)` = `node.getRootNode()` if its nodeType is 11 (ShadowRoot) or 9 (Document), else `document`. `ruleIndex(scope)` builds, once per scope, an array of `{rule, media, selectorText, tokens, isState, starting}`. Rules with no selectorText or an empty style block are skipped. `isState` = `ANY_STATE_RE.test(selectorText) || insideStartingStyleBlock`. Every consumer (statesFor, componentBaseRules, componentStateRules, ancestorContext) iterates this one array and filters. `invalidateRuleIndex()` (new WeakMap) is called at the end of every scan so a re-scan after DOM mutation is not stale. ShadowRoot exposes `.styleSheets` exactly like Document, so one code path serves both.
mechanisms.location: content.js ~4308-4346 (index + scopeOf), 4346 (invalidate)
mechanisms.chrome_apis_used: none (pure DOM/CSSOM), except that reaching CLOSED shadow roots needs chrome.dom.openOrClosedShadowRoot elsewhere
mechanisms.electron_equivalent: Identical DOM code, run inside the guest via `webContents.executeJavaScript` or a preload-installed function. For CLOSED shadow roots (where `getRootNode()` still works from inside, but you cannot get a handle from outside) use CDP `DOM.getDocument({depth:-1, pierce:true})` via `webContents.debugger` — it returns closed roots with `shadowRootType:"closed"`.
mechanisms.port_notes: Keep the WeakMap-by-scope design verbatim; it is the single highest-leverage idea here. In Electron add a second cache layer in the MAIN process keyed by (url, sheet href, etag) so re-opening the same page in the mini-browser does not re-walk.
mechanisms.which_deliverable: (a) builder — this is how a captured component gets its CSS; also (c) picker

mechanisms.name: Selector-token pre-filter (the reason it is not quadratic)
mechanisms.problem: Testing every rule against every node with `matches()` is millions of calls on a utility-CSS site. But you cannot skip rules blindly without losing real matches.
mechanisms.how_it_works: For each rule, `selectorTokens(sel)` extracts three token kinds into a Set: class tokens via `/\.((?:\\.|[-\w])+)/g` (backslash escapes stripped, stored as `.name`), id tokens via `/#([-\w]+)/g` (stored `#name`), and tag tokens via `/(?:^|[\s>+~,(])([a-zA-Z][\w-]*)/g` lowercased. For the subtree, `subtreeTokens(nodes)` collects tagName.toLowerCase(), `#id`, and every classList entry as `.cls`. `sharesToken(ruleTokens, have)` returns true if ANY token intersects. A rule whose tokens are ALL absent cannot possibly match, so it is never `matches()`-tested. Deliberately an over-approximation: the element a rule paints is always inside the subtree, so its tokens are always present — nothing that truly matches is lost, only false positives survive to the (cheap) matches() stage.
mechanisms.location: content.js ~4270-4307 (selectorTokens, subtreeTokens, sharesToken)
mechanisms.electron_equivalent: none needed — pure JS
mechanisms.port_notes: Note the subtle bug surface: attribute selectors (`[data-foo]`) produce no token, so such rules are token-empty and `sharesToken` returns false — they are silently dropped. Fix on the way over: treat a token-less selector as ALWAYS a candidate (fall through to matches()).

mechanisms.name: eachStyleRule — the CSSOM walker that survives modern CSS
mechanisms.problem: A naive `for (sheet of styleSheets) for (rule of sheet.cssRules)` loses: nested rules (`&:hover` inside a rule), CSSNestedDeclarations (Chrome 130+), @starting-style entry values, constructed stylesheets, and cross-origin sheets (which throw).
mechanisms.how_it_works: Recursive `walk(rules, media, depth, parentSel, starting)` capped at depth 8. Four cases per rule, in order: (1) rule HAS `.style` with declarations but NO `selectorText` and there IS a parentSel -> this is a CSSNestedDeclarations node (declarations written AFTER a nested rule); emit it under the parent's selector, otherwise it vanishes silently. (2) rule has selectorText + style -> resolve nesting via `resolveNesting(sel, parentSel)`: no parent -> sel; parent and no `&` -> `parentSel + " " + sel` (implicit descendant); parent with `&` -> `sel.replace(/&/g, ":is(" + parentSel + ")")` — the `:is()` wrap is what preserves correctness when the parent is a group. Emit, then recurse into `rule.cssRules` with sel as the new parent (this is where `&:hover` lives). (3) grouping rule -> compute `cond = rule.conditionText || rule.media?.mediaText || ""`, recurse with `media = media ? media + " and " + cond : cond`, and propagate `starting = starting || isStartingStyleRule(rule)`. @starting-style is detected by `rule.constructor.name === "CSSStartingStyleRule"` with a `/^@starting-style/i.test(cssText.slice(0,20))` fallback. Sheet enumeration: `Array.from(scope.styleSheets)` first, each `sheet.cssRules` in a try/catch (cross-origin throws SecurityError -> the sheet is silently skipped), THEN `scope.adoptedStyleSheets` walked LAST because constructed sheets cascade after the document's own — source order in the emitted array IS the cascade model.
mechanisms.location: content.js ~4351-4420 (eachStyleRule, resolveNesting, isStartingStyleRule)
mechanisms.electron_equivalent: Same code. The cross-origin hole is the thing that changes: in Electron you can (a) refetch the sheet from the MAIN process with `net.fetch` / Node fetch — no CORS exists there at all — and re-parse it with a CSS parser, or (b) use CDP `CSS.getStyleSheetText(styleSheetId)` after `CSS.enable`, which returns the text of cross-origin sheets, or (c) tap `session.webRequest.onCompleted` / a `protocol` handler to keep every stylesheet body as it loads.
mechanisms.port_notes: PORT the walker verbatim, then ADD a cross-origin path. Today a component whose CSS comes from a CDN sheet without CORS headers extracts to nothing — and the documented 'fallback to computed styles' does NOT actually save it, because statesFor also reads only the rule index. This is the single biggest fidelity gap in the extension and Electron erases it for free.

mechanisms.name: Condition folding bug: @supports and @container are re-emitted as @media
mechanisms.problem: Grouping rules other than @media carry their condition in `conditionText` too. The walker folds them all into one `media` string, and the emitter unconditionally wraps that string in `@media { }`.
mechanisms.how_it_works: In eachStyleRule: `const cond = rule.conditionText || rule.media?.mediaText || ""` — CSSSupportsRule and CSSContainerRule both inherit `conditionText` from CSSConditionRule, so `@supports (backdrop-filter: blur(1px))` yields cond = `(backdrop-filter: blur(1px))`, and `@container (min-width: 400px)` yields `(min-width: 400px)`. In componentCss the emission is `if (r.media) lines.push(\`@media ${r.media} {\`)`. Result: a supports-gated rule is exported as `@media (backdrop-filter: blur(1px)) { ... }` (a media query that never matches -> the rule is dead in the copy), and a container query is exported as a viewport media query (fires at the wrong times). @layer is worse: CSSLayerBlockRule has neither conditionText nor media, so `cond` is "" and the layer wrapper is simply DROPPED — layered rules are flattened to normal priority and can now beat rules they used to lose to. IDEAS.md #2 explicitly names container-query context as one of the five things a snipped element loses; the code does not implement it.
mechanisms.location: content.js ~4400-4404 (folding) and ~6594-6597 / ~6618-6625 (emission)
mechanisms.electron_equivalent: none needed — fix in our own code
mechanisms.port_notes: Carry conditions as a typed stack `[{kind:'media'|'supports'|'container'|'layer', text, name}]` instead of a concatenated string, and re-emit each wrapper with its own at-rule. For container queries also lift `container-type`/`container-name` off the nearest declaring ancestor onto the generated `.parent` wrapper — that is exactly what IDEAS.md #2 asks for and it is the missing piece that makes a copied responsive component behave.

mechanisms.name: componentBaseRules — resting appearance, authored not computed
mechanisms.problem: Computed styles flatten `var()` references, lose shorthands, lose author intent, and must be captured per-node for every descendant. The authored rules already carry all of it.
mechanisms.how_it_works: Subtree = `[root, ...root.querySelectorAll('*').slice(0, 80)]`. Iterate the rule index; skip `isState` rules (handled separately); skip on token miss; hard cap at 120 collected rules (deliberately generous because a shadow-scoped sheet ships its own CSS reset BEFORE the component's rules, and source order IS the cascade — you cannot reorder the reset away). For each rule, split `selectorText` on ',' and test EVERY part, not just the first (keeping only the first part silently stripped siblings: `.core, .action { border-radius: 50% }` exported as `.core` alone and the action buttons came out square). Per part: `stripHost()` to remove `:host`/`:host()`/`:host-context()`; drop parts starting `*`/`html`/`body` (universal resets are not the component); `matchableSelector()` to strip pseudo-ELEMENTS (`::before` etc.) since no node can ever match them; then `subtree.some(n => n.matches(mSel))`. Surviving parts are re-joined with ', ' so the exported selector is the author's group minus the parts that do not apply here. Declarations come from `ruleCssText(rule, sampleMatching(subtree, parts[0]))`. Dedup key is `selector + '|' + css`.
mechanisms.location: content.js ~4868-4920 (componentBaseRules), 4479-4487 (stripHost), 4498-4500 (matchableSelector)
mechanisms.electron_equivalent: none needed
mechanisms.port_notes: The 80-descendant and 120-rule caps are the tuning knobs; on desktop with a worker you can raise both. Keep the group-splitting behaviour — it is a bug fix someone paid for in blood.

mechanisms.name: ruleCssText — the CSSOM shorthand-with-var() serialization hole
mechanisms.problem: A shorthand holding a custom property cannot be serialized by the CSSOM. `border: 4px solid var(--line)` reads back as fifteen EMPTY longhands, and `style.cssText` emits `border-top-width: ;` — not merely lossy, but INVALID CSS that kills the whole rule when pasted. Asking for the shorthand does not help: `border`, `border-width`, `border-style`, `border-color` all return "".
mechanisms.how_it_works: Fast path: if `!/:\s*(;|$)/.test(style.cssText)` (no empty value anywhere) return cssText untouched — the author's exact text. Slow path: get `getComputedStyle(sampleEl)` where sampleEl is a node the rule actually paints (found by `sampleMatching(subtree, sel)` = first node matching the pseudo-element-stripped selector). Then iterate `style[i]` by index; value = `style.getPropertyValue(prop) || computed.getPropertyValue(prop)`; if still empty, DROP the declaration rather than emit `prop: ;`. Re-append ` !important` from `getPropertyPriority(prop)`. Critically, for STATE rules `sampleEl` is passed as `null` on purpose — a state rule is read off an element that is NOT in that state, so a computed fallback would fill the blanks with resting values and silently invert the state.
mechanisms.location: content.js ~4807-4840 (ruleCssText), 4860-4866 (sampleMatching), 4982 (the null-sample decision)
mechanisms.electron_equivalent: none needed for the fallback; but CDP `CSS.getMatchedStylesForNode` returns each rule's ORIGINAL source text ranges (`CSS.getStyleSheetText` + range) which sidesteps the CSSOM re-serialization entirely and gives byte-identical author CSS.
mechanisms.port_notes: Keep this as the fallback, but make CDP source-range extraction the primary path in Electron — it is strictly better: no re-serialization, comments preserved, `var()` preserved, shorthands preserved. Keep the `sampleEl = null` rule for state rules under both paths.

mechanisms.name: componentStateRules — capturing :hover/:focus/open without ever touching the page
mechanisms.problem: getComputedStyle only ever reports the moment you asked. A button's hover colour, a card's lift, a menu's open state — none of it is applied while you copy, so every tool on the market produces a dead copy. Nothing may be clicked, hovered or mutated on the user's page.
mechanisms.how_it_works: Read what COULD apply instead of what IS applied. `ANY_STATE_RE` is one composed regex covering: `:hover|:focus|:active|:disabled|:checked|:visited|:invalid|:focus-visible|:focus-within|:open|:popover-open`, `[data-state`, `[data-(open|expanded|active|selected|checked|visible)]`, `[aria-(expanded|selected|current|invalid|pressed|checked|hidden)]`, `[disabled]`, `[open]`, `.is-(open|active|expanded|visible|selected|checked)`, plus `OPEN_CLASS_RE = /\.[a-zA-Z][\w-]*\.(?:open|opened|expanded|collapsed|shown|menu-open|nav-open|is-open)\b/`. That last one is COMPOUNDED only (`.nav-dropdown.open`, never a bare `.open`) — bare `.open`/`.active`/`.show`/`.selected` are deliberately excluded because half the web uses them for the current tab or nav link, and moving those out of the resting rules leaves ordinary elements previewing unstyled. Matching: strip the state condition with `baseSelector()` (`.btn:hover .icon` -> `.btn .icon`), strip pseudo-elements with `matchableSelector()`, then `subtree.some(matches)`. If that misses, fall back to `subjectCompound(sel)` — everything after the last TOP-LEVEL combinator, computed by scanning with a bracket-depth counter so combinators inside `:not(...)`/`:has(...)` do not count. That fallback exists because stripping a state out of a functional pseudo INVERTS it: `.rail:not(:has(button:hover)) button` becomes `.rail:not(:has(button)) button`, which a rail that always contains a button can never match. Over-approximating is safe here because the rule ships verbatim — worst case is exporting a rule that never fires. Grouped selectors are part-filtered exactly as in the base pass.
mechanisms.location: content.js ~4930-4992 (componentStateRules), 4212-4262 (STATE_PATTERNS/ANY_STATE_RE/OPEN_CLASS_RE), 4518-4546 (baseSelector), 4848-4858 (subjectCompound)
mechanisms.electron_equivalent: none needed. CDP offers `CSS.forcePseudoState(nodeId, ['hover','active','focus'])` which would let you ACTUALLY render each state and screenshot it — something the extension can never do without mutating the user's page. In our own mini-browser that is legitimate.
mechanisms.port_notes: Port the static harvest as-is (it is the safe, fast path), then ADD a CDP `forcePseudoState` + `capturePage` verification pass in the mini-browser: force :hover, screenshot, compare to the exported copy rendered in our sandbox. That turns 'looks plausible' into 'proven identical' and is the verification moat IDEAS.md keeps arguing for. Also: baseSelector MUST stay a mirror of ANY_STATE_RE — every marker the regex recognises has to be strippable here, or the rule is filed as a state and then fails the very match test that filing it there was meant to let it pass.

mechanisms.name: Pseudo-element survival (::before/::after are usually the entire design)
mechanisms.problem: A pseudo-element is not a node, so `el.matches('.btn::after')` is ALWAYS false and every such rule used to be discarded — taking with it the glows, overlays, sliding fills and decorative shapes that are frequently the whole visual design.
mechanisms.how_it_works: Three cooperating pieces. (1) `PSEUDO_EL_RE = /::?(before|after|first-line|first-letter|placeholder|selection|marker|backdrop|file-selector-button)\b(\([^)]*\))?/g` and `matchableSelector(sel)` strips them ONLY for the matching question — the rule is still exported with the author's original selector intact. So matching asks the answerable question ('does this rule apply to something in the subtree?') while export keeps fidelity. (2) `TRAILING_PSEUDO_RE` (same list, anchored `$`) + `applyState(sel, cond)` inserts a state condition BEFORE the trailing pseudo: `.btn` + `:hover` + `::after` -> `.btn:hover::after`, because `.btn::after:hover` matches nothing. (3) `pseudoOf(sel)` returns `'::before'`/`'::after'` so `getComputedStyle(el, pseudo)` can be used to read pseudo values. Asset extraction separately reads `getComputedStyle(elm, '::before'|'::after')` for `content`, `backgroundImage` and `maskImage` url()s on the first 2500 elements.

mechanisms.electron_equivalent: none needed. CDP `CSS.getMatchedStylesForNode` returns `pseudoElements[]` with their matched rules explicitly, which is cleaner than regex surgery.
mechanisms.port_notes: Keep applyState (state-before-pseudo ordering is a correctness rule, not a heuristic). Replace the strip-and-match dance with CDP's pseudoElements array where available; keep the regex path as the no-debugger fallback.

mechanisms.name: ancestorContext — custom properties lifted from AUTHORED rules, not computed values
mechanisms.problem: A snipped element loses inherited text styles, the CSS variables its rules depend on, the theme classes its rules key off, and the parent layout mode that decides its size. Naively you would read variables from getComputedStyle — but that returns the RESOLVED value (`rgb(79,70,229)`), never the `var(--brand)` reference that produced it. Flattening to constants destroys re-theming and silently kills some animations.
mechanisms.how_it_works: Four independent harvests merged into one object. (1) INHERITED: `getComputedStyle(el)` for a fixed 13-property list (font-family, font-size, font-weight, font-style, line-height, letter-spacing, color, text-align, direction, white-space, text-transform, word-spacing, list-style). (2) VARS — a two-source join: the REFERENCES live only in authored rules, the VALUES live only in computed style. Pass A: for every rule in the scope's index that shares a token with the subtree AND whose `style.cssText` contains 'var(', check whether any selector part matches something in `[el, ...el.querySelectorAll('*').slice(0,60)]`; if so, collect every `var(--name` occurrence via `/var\(\s*(--[\w-]+)/g`. Pass B: eachStyleRule NEVER yields @keyframes, so a dot whose colour is only set at `66% { background: var(--wire) }` exported unresolved and played to transparent — measured at 12 of 94 keyframes in one motion library. So: collect `getComputedStyle(n).animationName` for every subtree node, `keyframesText(name, scope)` for each, and regex the same var() references out of the keyframe text. Then RESOLVE: `getComputedStyle(el).getPropertyValue(name)` for each collected name, and follow indirection up to depth 3 (a token defined in terms of another token). (3) ANCESTOR CLASSES: walk up max 12 levels (stopping at documentElement), take up to 4 classes per level, keep only those matching `/dark|light|theme|rtl|ltr|mode/i`. (4) PARENT LAYOUT: if the parent's computed `display` matches `/flex|grid/`, capture display, flexDirection, gap, alignItems, justifyContent, gridTemplateColumns. (5) BACKDROP: walk up to 12 ancestors — crossing shadow boundaries via `a.getRootNode().host` where `parentElement` stops — and take the first backgroundColor that is not transparent/`rgba(0,0,0,0)`, so the preview paints the surface the component was designed against (a dark component on white is invisible).

Also missing: `container-type`/`container-name` on ancestors (needed for the @container fix above). In Electron the resolution loop is free to be exhaustive since there is no message-port budget.

mechanisms.name: @property registration harvest (the silent-failure guard)
mechanisms.problem: An UNREGISTERED custom property animates DISCRETELY — it snaps between keyframes instead of interpolating. Drop the @property registration and the copy is pixel-correct at rest and visibly wrong in motion, with no error, no warning, nothing in the console. IDEAS.md calls this the most dangerous silent failure in the whole list.
mechanisms.how_it_works: `propertyRules(scope)` walks styleSheets + adoptedStyleSheets to depth 6, identifying a registration by `rule.constructor.name === 'CSSPropertyRule'` with a `/^@property/i.test(cssText.slice(0,10))` fallback, and returns a `Map(name -> cssText)`. In the component pipeline: `propertyBlocks = Object.keys(context.vars).map(n => registered.get(n)).filter(Boolean)` — i.e. only registrations for tokens this component actually uses. componentCss emits them FIRST, before anything that uses them, because an @property must be seen before the value it types is used.

mechanisms.name: componentCss — the assembly order (this order is load-bearing)
mechanisms.problem: Emitting the right rules in the wrong order produces CSS that is individually correct and collectively wrong.

(7) transitions — but ONLY if no base rule already carried a `transition` declaration for the element itself. (8) state rules verbatim, each re-wrapped in `@starting-style { }` if `r.starting`, because emitted bare those values (which the element animates FROM on insertion) would paint the entry frame permanently. mechanisms.name: Icon reproduction: render the glyph from the font, else crop the screenshot
mechanisms.problem: An icon-font icon and a CSS-mask icon have NO file to download. Every asset extractor returns nothing for them, and they are usually the most reusable art on the page.

TIER 1 `renderGlyph(text, family, color)`: `unquoteContent()` first turns a computed `content` value into real text — strips the quotes, rejects anything containing `url(`/`attr(`/`counter(`, and decodes CSS escapes with `/\\([0-9a-f]{1,6})\s?/gi -> String.fromCodePoint(parseInt(hex,16))` (that decode is what turns `\e903` into the actual PBF codepoint). Then `document.fonts.load('64px ' + family, text)`, measure with a 2D context: if width is falsy or > 64*1.7 the font did NOT substitute a ligature and we would be drawing the literal WORD, so bail. Otherwise draw at 256x256, font-size 0.76*256, centred, baseline middle, y = 0.54*256, fill colour = the element's own colour unless transparent. Verify by sampling the alpha channel every 40 bytes: fewer than 10 inked samples means a missing glyph (tofu draws nothing) -> return null. Only then `toDataURL('image/png')`. TIER 2, for candidates that failed tier 1 AND are fully within the viewport: hide the picker's own overlay, wait 60ms, `chrome.runtime.sendMessage({type:'CAPTURE_TAB'})`, load the returned dataUrl into an Image, and for each icon crop `(rect.left - 2) * devicePixelRatio` etc. onto a canvas sized to the DPR-scaled rect. That is CORRECT as long as (1) nothing was dropped, (2) nothing was reordered, and (3) no @layer was flattened — the 120-rule cap and the @layer drop both violate it. The 120 cap is explicitly generous 'because a shadow-scoped sheet ships its own CSS reset ahead of the component's rules, and source order is the cascade — the reset cannot be reordered away'.

mechanisms.name: Two-pass component detection with a wall-clock deadline and a drop ledger

Containment rule: `taken.some(t => t.contains(el))` rejects a piece of an already-listed component (the sliding fill inside a button belongs to the button) while ANCESTORS still pass (a card containing an accepted button is a different, larger thing). Final ordering computes `__depth` = the number of OTHER ACCEPTED components above this one, then sorts `a.__depth - b.__depth || b.rank - a.rank` — because a pairwise 'is an ancestor of' comparator is NOT transitive and Array.sort mangles it. Rank = paintScore + states.length*3 + (hasMotion ? 5 : 0) + (repeatedItem ? 12 : 0). Every rejection increments a named counter in a `dropped` object (`dupe`, `hidden`, `size`) which is returned to the panel and rendered in the status line as 'N of M candidates — excluded: X duplicate, Y hidden, Z too small'. An UNREGISTERED custom property animates DISCRETELY — it snaps between keyframes instead of interpolating. Drop the @property registration and the copy is pixel-perfect at rest and visibly wrong in motion, with no error anywhere. Registrations must also be emitted BEFORE any value they type.

The `animation` shorthand RESETS every sub-property it omits. Restating an animation the author already declared turns `forwards` into `none`, and an element written `opacity: 0` and revealed by a forwards animation then stays invisible forever. componentCss guards this with authoredAnimation(trigger), which checks base rules AND the state rule for the same trigger — checking only baseRules let a recorded :hover animation replace an authored `.btn:hover { animation: pulse … infinite }` and the shorthand reset turned an infinite pulse into a single pass frozen on its last frame.

A shorthand holding a custom property CANNOT be serialized by the CSSOM. `border: 4px solid var(--line)` reads back as fifteen empty longhands and cssText emits `border-top-width: ;` — invalid CSS that kills the entire rule when pasted. `border`, `border-width`, `border-style` and `border-color` ALL return "". The only recovery is getComputedStyle on an element the rule actually paints.

That computed-style recovery must NOT be used for state rules: a state rule is read off an element that is not in that state, so the fallback silently fills blanks with resting values. componentStateRules passes sampleEl = null deliberately.

@starting-style is a state by POSITION, not by selector — its selector is an ordinary one, so a pseudo-class test rejects it. It must be flagged during the walk and re-wrapped on emission, or the values the element animates FROM on insertion are painted permanently.

CSSNestedDeclarations (Chrome 130+): declarations written AFTER a nested rule are parked in a rule that has a `.style` but NO `selectorText`. A walker that keys on selectorText drops them without a trace. Detect: style.length > 0 && !selectorText && parentSel exists -> attribute to parentSel.

Nested `&` must be resolved as `:is(parentSel)`, not by string substitution of the parent, or a grouped parent selector changes meaning. No `&` at all means implicit descendant: `parentSel + ' ' + sel`.

A pseudo-element is not a node — `el.matches('.btn::after')` is always false. Strip pseudo-elements for the MATCH question only; export the author's selector untouched. And a state condition goes BEFORE the trailing pseudo: `.btn:hover::after` is the rule, `.btn::after:hover` matches nothing.

Stripping a state condition out of a functional pseudo INVERTS the selector: `.rail:not(:has(button:hover)) button` becomes `.rail:not(:has(button)) button`, which a rail that always contains a button can never match — the rule was silently discarded. Fix: also test the SUBJECT COMPOUND (everything after the last top-level combinator, found with a bracket-depth scan so combinators inside :not()/:has() do not count). Over-approximating is safe because the rule ships verbatim.

baseSelector() must strip EVERY marker that ANY_STATE_RE recognises. Otherwise a rule is filed as a state and then fails the very match test that filing it there was meant to let it pass — strictly worse than leaving it a resting rule.

Bare `.open` / `.active` / `.show` / `.selected` are DELIBERATELY excluded from the open-state regex: half the web uses them for the current tab or nav link, and treating them as states moves ordinary layout rules out of the resting set, leaving such elements previewing unstyled. Only COMPOUNDED markers count (`.nav-dropdown.open`, never a bare `.open`). `.active` is excluded even compounded — it almost always marks the current tab and it is the one marker with real reach.

A grouped selector can paint several elements of the same component and every matching part must survive. Keeping only the first match exported `.demo-orbit-core, .demo-orbit-action { border-radius: 50% }` as `.demo-orbit-core` alone, so the action buttons came out square; and a grouped state rule pairing hover with its resting counterpart lost the default, so the item highlighted at rest came out plain.

The 120-rule cap in componentBaseRules is deliberately generous because a shadow-scoped stylesheet ships its own CSS reset BEFORE the component's rules, and source order IS the cascade — the reset cannot be reordered away or the copy renders wrong.

Indexing only `document` returns ZERO CSS for component showcases (uiverse.io and similar), which give every item its own shadow root with its own <style>. The rule index MUST be keyed per tree scope. Same for @keyframes: search the element's own scope first, then fall back to document.
adoptedStyleSheets cascade AFTER the document's own sheets, so they must be walked LAST. The walk order is the cascade model — there is no specificity computation anywhere in this codebase.

Cross-origin stylesheets throw on `.cssRules` and are silently skipped by the component path (only the asset/clone paths re-fetch them). The documented 'fall back to reconstructing states from the computed-style summary' does NOT rescue this, because statesFor also reads only the rule index. A page whose CSS is served from a no-CORS CDN currently extracts to nothing.

@supports and @container conditions are folded into the same string as @media and re-emitted as `@media (...)` — a supports-gated rule becomes a media query that never matches (dead in the copy) and a container query becomes a viewport query (fires at the wrong times). @layer is dropped entirely, flattening layered rules to normal priority.

componentCss NEVER emits an @font-face rule. @font-face is harvested (scanStylesheets) but used only to label files in the assets tab, so a captured component that uses a webfont exports with `font-family: 'Inter'` and no font behind it.

IDEAS.md #23 (content-addressed asset dedup via SubtleCrypto) is SCORED BUT NOT IMPLEMENTED — there is no crypto.subtle, no digest(), no hash function anywhere in content.js, sidepanel.js or background.js. All dedup is by URL string, by whitespace-normalised SVG markup, or by hand-rolled concatenated fingerprints. libId had to have the component's own text appended to it because 144 same-sized cards from one page collided on name+kind+w+h+cssLen+htmlLen.
A pairwise 'is an ancestor of' comparator is NOT transitive and Array.sort mangles it. Sort by ancestor COUNT (number of other accepted components above this one) instead.

`sandbox=""` on an iframe makes it cross-origin, and a cross-origin frame CONSUMES the click — the containing card receives no click event at all (measured, not assumed). The workaround is listening for window `blur` and checking whether document.activeElement is a preview frame; and blur() on the frame does not move focus out, you must focus something else.

Preview scale is capped at 84% of the box, never enlarged: glows, badges and outlines drawn by ::before/::after live OUTSIDE the element's own box and a 100% fit shaves them off; a 20px switch blown up looks broken. The inner wrapper needs `width:max-content;height:max-content` or a component wider than the thumbnail is laid out against the left edge and clipped on one side when scaled about its centre. And `place-content` is required alongside `place-items` or the grid track itself is not centred.

The preview's backdrop must be the surface the component actually sat on (walk up to 12 ancestors for the first non-transparent backgroundColor, crossing shadow boundaries via getRootNode().host where parentElement stops) — a dark component previewed against white is invisible.

Anything crossing from the page's own world is hostile input. Event-listener TYPE names are filtered with /^[A-Za-z][\w.:-]{0,39}$/ specifically because a page registering `` as a listener type would otherwise have that string emitted into the exported CSS and into the bundle the user pastes. The CSS comment listing them additionally strips `<`, `>` and `*/`.

inert() is only two rules — `</script|</style` -> `<\/…` and `<!--` -> `<\!--` — and `type="text/plain"` on the handler block only holds as long as nothing in the body can close the tag, which is why the WHOLE body including event names is escaped.

cleanOuterHTML must run in verbatim mode for components: trimming to the first 8 classes silently breaks any utility-CSS component, and inline styles are often the entire design. Only `on*` attributes are unconditionally stripped.
`el.currentSrc` not `el.src` for images — it is the srcset variant the browser actually chose — and srcset must be REMOVED after rewriting src or the browser re-picks the original.
A data: URI typed `application/octet-stream` inlines fine but never renders; fetchAsDataUrl goes through blob -> FileReader specifically to preserve the response MIME type.

Canvas emptiness must be decided by INSPECTING PIXELS (sample the alpha channel; >4 means ink), never by the size of the exported data URL — a solid-colour canvas compresses to a tiny string. Same technique proves a rendered glyph is real: sample alpha every 40 bytes, require at least 10 inked samples, because a missing glyph draws nothing.
An icon-font ligature collapses to about 1em; if measureText width exceeds 64*1.7 the font did not substitute and you are about to draw the literal WORD instead of the icon. Bail.

A hidden element measures 0x0, so a bounding-rect test doubles as a visibility test — but for SVG you must then fall back to the width/height attributes or the viewBox, or hidden icons are dropped. And any SVG whose markup contains `<symbol` must be rejected outright, or that size fallback turns a sprite sheet into one enormous unusable 'icon'.
Pass 3 (live motion recording) is skipped when document.visibilityState !== 'visible' — rAF is frozen in a hidden tab, so the page's own spring engines cannot move and there is nothing to record.

Budgets that are actually in the code: rule index caps 120 base + 120 state rules per component; 80 descendants for base/state matching, 60 for var lifting, 200 for state scanning; 50 stylesheets scanned, 15 remote sheets refetched (4s timeout, 1.5 MB each), 20 for the clone path (8s, 3 MB each); deepAll 9000 nodes / depth 14; nesting walk depth 8; pass-2 deadline 8000 ms; motion record budget 90000 ms with 16 recordings and a 300-component listener probe; single-file clone MAX_IMG 2 MB with a 25 MB total budget; ZIP MAX_FILE 30 MB with a 300 MB budget; data: URLs capped at 2 MB (CSS) / 3 MB (DOM); component HTML truncated at 12000 chars; handler source at 1500 chars; chrome.storage.local library warns past 8 MB of a 10 MB ceiling.

Electron erases four of the extension's hardest constraints outright: no CORS on main-process fetch (cross-origin stylesheets become readable), a real filesystem (no base64 inlining, no hand-rolled ZIP writer, no 10 MB storage ceiling), preload scripts that run before every page script in a controlled world (a strictly better document_start hook than the extension had), and webContents.debugger/CDP which supplies getMatchedStylesForNode (cascade-ordered matched rules + the inherited ancestor chain + pseudo-element rules), getStyleSheetText (cross-origin source), DOM.getDocument({pierce:true}) (closed shadow roots, replacing chrome.dom.openOrClosedShadowRoot), forcePseudoState (actually render :hover for verification), Emulation.setDeviceMetricsOverride (real responsive reflow for the desktop/tablet/mobile switch, not a scaled screenshot), and capturePage (element screenshots without hiding an overlay or doing DPR arithmetic).

subsystem: Multi-pass UI scan + live behavior recorder (content.js v3.2.0, with hook.js MAIN-world registry)
summary: A three-pass pipeline that turns a live page into a list of exportable components with their states AND their motion. Pass 1 is a cheap whole-DOM triage (classify + paint-score + two-tier dedup) that scores everything before spending on anything. Pass 2 runs the "State Ghost" — reads every stylesheet rule carrying a state condition (:hover/:active/[data-state=open]/…), strips the condition, matches the remainder against the subtree, and diffs the declared values against the resting computed style, producing a (what you touch / what kind of touch / what changes) triple without mutating the page. Pass 3 is the headline: it physically performs hover-arc / press / click / drag on up to 16 components, samples getComputedStyle of up to 32 nodes every animation frame, and re-emits what moved as @keyframes — the only way to capture spring/JS-driven motion that exists in no stylesheet. Around Pass 3 sits an unusually careful safety machine (subtree-wide clickUnsafe vetting against real handler source read from a MAIN-world listener registry, an untrusted-event window guard, page "quiet mode" that blocks mutating requests/beacons/popups/pushState, and Escape-only-if-we-opened-something).

mechanisms.name: Pass 0 — materializeLazyContent (time-boxed scroll sweep)
mechanisms.problem: Component showcases mount items lazily on intersection, so scanning the page as-loaded finds mostly empty containers.
mechanisms.how_it_works: If scrollHeight <= innerHeight*1.5, return immediately (nothing below the fold). Otherwise compute step = max(400, round(innerHeight*0.9)) and loop y from 0 to min(scrollHeight, 60000) by step: window.scrollTo(0,y), await setTimeout 45ms, post a progress message with pct = y/h. Break the moment Date.now() exceeds a deadline (budgetMs default 12000) and set truncated=true. Then scrollTo(0, startY) and wait 250ms for the last mounts to settle. Time-boxed rather than run to completion on purpose: each stop costs whatever the page spends mounting, ~1s/screen on a heavy showcase, so an unbounded sweep of a long page hangs for minutes. The truncated flag is returned to the UI so a second scan can start from a different scroll position. Measured: uiverse.io goes from 1 mounted component to 34.
mechanisms.location: content.js:5409-5433 (helper); called from extractUiComponents at content.js:6292-6300
mechanisms.electron_equivalent: webContents.executeJavaScript of the same loop inside the guest, progress over ipcRenderer→webContents.send. Better: because we own the mini-browser, run the sweep with webContents.setZoomFactor/insets or just resize the WebContentsView tall (e.g. setBounds to full document height) and let everything intersect at once — no scrolling, no mount-cost-per-screen, no 12s budget. CDP Emulation.setDeviceMetricsOverride with a tall height does the same without touching real layout width.
mechanisms.port_notes: Keep the budget+truncated protocol; it is what stops a scan from hanging. Replace the scroll loop with a viewport-height override where possible. Also drop the visibility gate elsewhere by setting webPreferences.backgroundThrottling:false, otherwise a hidden WebContentsView freezes rAF exactly like a hidden tab.

mechanisms.name: Pass 1 — cheap triage: classify + paintScore over the whole deep DOM
mechanisms.problem: The old scan stopped at the first 40 matches in DOM order, so page furniture near the top filled the list and real components further down were never considered. Also: how do you tell a component from a layout wrapper?
mechanisms.how_it_works: deepAll() walks the document INCLUDING shadow roots. For each element: (1) getBoundingClientRect; reject if w<12 or h<10 UNLESS isDisclosureTarget(el) says a real disclosure control declares it (aria-controls+aria-expanded pointing at its id, previous sibling with aria-expanded, child of <details>, or a zero-height panel directly after a real button); (2) reject display:none/visibility:hidden/opacity:0 under the same exception; (3) classifyComponent(el, cs) walks an ordered COMPONENT_KINDS table (button, input, toggle, avatar, badge, loader, modal, menu, tabs, nav, card, form, table) matching on tag/role plus class WORDS — classes are split on -/_/camelCase into a word Set and compared as words, never substrings, because substring matching read the "item" inside Tailwind's `items-center` and filed every flex wrapper as a card. The last-resort kind "interactive" accepts anything with a non-zero transition/animation, an INTERACTIVE_CURSOR (pointer|grab|grabbing|crosshair|move|*-resize|zoom-*), or isDrawnSurface(cs) && housesMotion(el) — a painted+bordered/rounded/shadowed box holding motion in its first 12 descendants. That last clause exists because a drag pad is a bordered box whose 26px puck does the moving; testing the element's own motion rejected the pad and kept the puck. (4) paintScore: bg color +2, bg image +2, border +2, box-shadow +2, radius +1, cursor:pointer +2, transition +4, animation +4, native form tag +5 (or kind button/input/toggle +4), root is a ShadowRoot +4 (a showcase isolates each exhibit); penalties: area > 40% of viewport -8, > 18% -3, >40 descendants -4, >20 -2. Gate: score < 5 is rejected as scaffolding. The area penalty is SKIPPED for repeatedItem(el) — three or more siblings with the same tag+first-two-classes — because the viewport shrinks when the side panel opens, a gallery card then clears 40% of it, takes -8, and fails the gate, while the little buttons inside it score 16 and fill the list.
mechanisms.location: content.js:6318-6388 (pass), 5131-5300 (classifyComponent/paintScore/repeatedItem), 5471-5540 (isDisclosureTarget), 1221 (deepAll)
mechanisms.electron_equivalent: Runs unchanged inside the guest via preload or webContents.executeJavaScript. For our own generated projects the whole heuristic can be REPLACED by ground truth: the builder knows which nodes are components because it emitted them (data-studio-component ids).
mechanisms.port_notes: For deliverable (a), keep this only as the 'import an arbitrary page' path. Inside our own builder, mark components at emit time and skip triage entirely. Note the viewport-relative area penalty is inherently unstable — viewArea = innerWidth*innerHeight changes when a panel opens; in Electron use the WebContentsView's own bounds, which we control and can hold constant.

mechanisms.name: Pass 1 dedup — two-tier signature escalation (the fix that recovered 7→144 cards)
mechanisms.problem: Ten identical buttons are one component, not ten. But a motion gallery's cards are identical by tag+class+height while each demonstrates a DIFFERENT effect, and the whole gallery collapsed to a handful of entries.
mechanisms.how_it_works: Group key sig = `${kind}|${TAG}|${first 4 plain class names}|${round(height)}`, where only /^[a-zA-Z_][\w-]*$/ classes count (analytics classes like `plausible-event-effect=Card+Resize` are unique per instance and would defeat dedup entirely). Each group holds {motions:Set, keys:Set, deep:bool}. Member key starts as motionSignature(el) alone: concatenate, over the first 24 descendants, '@'+animationName when not none and '~'+transitionProperty+transitionDuration when the property is neither 'all' nor 'none'. On an ordinary page every member hashes to the SAME empty string and collapses exactly as before. Only once a group has seen >= 3 DISTINCT motion signatures is it declared a gallery of effects (group.deep = true), and only then does the key escalate to motion + '||' + structureSignature(el) — '#'+descendant count then, per first 24 descendants, TAG + '.' + first two valid classes (text deliberately excluded: differing text is data, not structure; SVG className is an SVGAnimatedString so .baseVal is unwrapped). Hard cap of 300 keys per group. Measured: developer.mozilla.org grows 0%, kinetics.colorion.co goes from 7 cards to all 144. Tried and REJECTED: adding structure unconditionally (inflates MDN 62-74%) and adding child count to the key (MDN +61%).
mechanisms.location: content.js:6353-6386 (escalation), 5439-5470 (motionSignature/structureSignature)
mechanisms.electron_equivalent: none needed — pure DOM.
mechanisms.port_notes: This is the single most transferable idea in Pass 1: a cheap signature that is inert on normal content, escalating to an expensive one only for the group that proved it needs it. Same trick applies to our layers panel and to de-duplicating traced vector paths.

mechanisms.name: Pass 2 — State Ghost: the hover/focus/active/open state matrix (IDEAS.md #1, 8.7 — SHIPPED)
mechanisms.problem: getComputedStyle only ever reports the moment you asked. A button's hover colour, a card's lift, an open menu — none of it is applied while you copy, so every competing tool produces a dead copy.
mechanisms.how_it_works: Never touches the page. Instead of reading what IS applied it reads what COULD apply. A pre-built rule index (split into resting vs state rules by ANY_STATE_RE, each entry carrying selectorTokens for a fast pre-filter) is walked; a rule is skipped unless its class/id/tag tokens intersect the subtree's tokens (over-approximation on purpose — the painted element is always inside the subtree, so nothing that truly matches is lost; without it a Tailwind-sized sheet means millions of matches() calls). For each of 13 STATE_PATTERNS (hover, focus, focus-visible, focus-within, active, disabled, checked, [data-state=open], [aria-expanded=true], [aria-selected=true], [aria-current], invalid, visited) the rule's selectorText is split on commas and only the comma-parts that actually carry the state are used. baseSelector(sel) strips every state marker ANY_STATE_RE can capture, matchableSelector() additionally strips the pseudo-ELEMENT tail (no node can match ::after), and the remainder is run as root.matches() || root.querySelectorAll(). triggerSelector(sel, re) recovers WHICH element you have to touch; suffix = base.slice(trigger.length) recovers WHAT changes (appending the full base instead rebuilt the trigger twice: `.card:hover .card .title`). Declarations are then DIFFED against the resting computed style of a matching sample — read through the correct pseudo-element via getComputedStyle(sample, pseudoOf(target)) — and a declaration equal to its resting value is dropped, so "changes" means changed and not merely re-stated. STATE_PROPS includes `animation`, because a state that starts a keyframe animation is the most expressive kind and never runs at rest; stateKeyframesFor() then pulls those @keyframes bodies (including from adopted/shadow sheets) so the copy can actually replay them. ANY_STATE_RE deliberately EXCLUDES bare `.open`/`.active`/`.show`/`.selected` and accepts class-toggled open states only when compounded onto another class (`.nav-dropdown.open`), because half the web uses `.active` for the current tab and moving those rules out of the resting set leaves ordinary elements previewing unstyled. Measured on the widening: kinetics moves 20 rules (1.95%), MDN 8 (1.68%), all genuine open states, zero false positives.

mechanisms.chrome_apis_used: chrome.dom.openOrClosedShadowRoot (extension-only, no permission) to reach CLOSED shadow roots, with fallback to el.shadowRoot
mechanisms.electron_equivalent: Two options, and the second is strictly better: (1) port the CSSOM walker verbatim — document.styleSheets + adoptedStyleSheets work identically in Electron. (2) REBUILD on CDP via webContents.debugger: CSS.getMatchedStylesForNode returns matched rules with their pseudo-class rules and inherited chain already resolved, and CSS.forcePseudoState({nodeId, forcedPseudoClasses:['hover','active','focus','focus-visible']}) lets you FORCE the state and then read the real computed style — the State Ghost done by the engine, with zero selector parsing and no false matches. Closed shadow roots: DOM.getDocument({pierce:true}) returns them (chrome.dom has no Electron equivalent).
mechanisms.port_notes: Keep the OUTPUT SHAPE exactly — the (trigger element / trigger kind / target element / prop from→to) quadruple is the real invention, and the diff-against-resting rule is what makes it truthful. Replace the acquisition layer with CSS.forcePseudoState + CSS.getComputedStyleForNode. Keep baseSelector/triggerSelector for EMITTING the CSS we own. Keep the deliberate exclusion of bare `.active`/`.open` — it is a measured decision, not timidity.

mechanisms.name: Pass 2 — subsumption, depth-ordering and the exhibit-vs-part rank fix
mechanisms.problem: Two ordering bugs: a piece of an already-listed component was listed again as its own (empty) component, and the inner puck of a demo outranked the demo card it belongs to (card at position 159, 26px button at position 1).
mechanisms.how_it_works: Candidates are sorted by paint score and only the top limit*3 enter Pass 2, under an 8s deadline (opts.pass2Ms) after which pass2Cut=true is reported rather than hanging the page. A running `taken` array holds accepted elements; a candidate is skipped if any taken element .contains() it — descendants of an accepted component are not components (the sliding fill inside a button is an empty box on its own), while ANCESTORS still pass (a card containing an accepted button is a different, larger thing). rank = paintScore + states.length*3 + (hasMotion ? 5 : 0) + (repeatedItem ? 12 : 0) — a gallery exhibit is what the page is ABOUT. Final ordering is NOT a pairwise ancestor comparator (not transitive; Array.sort mangles it) but a precomputed depth: __depth = number of OTHER accepted components strictly above this element, then sort by (__depth asc, rank desc). Measured: first 144 gallery positions all become cards (first non-card at index 144); XY Pad card 159→48, its puck 1→174. __el/__depth/rank are deleted before returning because DOM handles cannot cross the message port.

mechanisms.electron_equivalent: none needed. The message-port constraint disappears — Electron IPC also cannot carry DOM handles, so the delete-before-return discipline stays.
mechanisms.port_notes: The transitivity note is the load-bearing part: any tree-ordering of picked elements in our layers panel must precompute a depth key, never use a pairwise contains() comparator.

mechanisms.name: Pass 2 — platform completeness: @property, @starting-style, scroll timelines, nested CSS, adopted sheets
mechanisms.problem: An exported component was right at rest and wrong in motion, or invisible, because five modern CSS platform features were silently dropped.
mechanisms.how_it_works: eachStyleRule descends into NESTED rules and resolves `&` against the parent, and synthesises an entry for CSSNestedDeclarations (a rule with no selector holding the declarations that follow the first nested rule) — it deliberately calls the visitor twice for a nested rule (parent, then the trailing declaration block) because each carries different declarations. propertyRules(scope) collects @property registrations and componentCss emits the ones registering variables the component uses — without them an animated custom property SNAPS between keyframes instead of interpolating. timelineRules() hoists the ANCESTOR's rule that defines the view-timeline-name/scroll-timeline-name the component consumes (scanned out of `animation-timeline: --x` in the component's own rules). @starting-style blocks are accepted without a state marker in the selector and re-wrapped on export (without the wrapper an element written opacity:0 and revealed by the animation stays invisible). ruleCssText() fills empty shorthand branches from getComputedStyle of a matching element, because a shorthand containing a var() (`border: 4px solid var(--line)`) returns 15 EMPTY longhands and cssText emits invalid `border-top-width: ;` — but a sample element is deliberately NOT passed for STATE rules, since reading a hover rule off an element that is not hovered yields resting values and corrupts the export. Measured: MDN 475→475 rules and Tailwind Docs 6082→6082 (zero inflation), 160/294 nested selectors actually resolved, 2 real @starting-style found on tailwindcss.com.

mechanisms.name: hook.js — MAIN-world listener registry (document_start monkeypatch of addEventListener)
mechanisms.problem: An isolated content script cannot see the page's event listeners at all. Without them there is no way to know whether a component is JS-driven, no way to rank recording slots, and no way to prove a click is safe.
mechanisms.how_it_works: Injected into the page's own world at document_start, before any page script. Guards re-entry with a Symbol.for('aiep.hook') on window. Keeps REG: WeakMap<EventTarget, Map<type, Set<handler>>>. Patches EventTarget.prototype.addEventListener/removeEventListener; the patch calls through to the originals. Three memory rules: `once:true` listeners are NOT stored (the browser removes them without ever calling removeEventListener, so storing them pins dead closures and the per-type cap then starts rejecting live ones); an AbortSignal gets an 'abort' cleanup registered through the ORIGINAL addEventListener and holding a WeakRef to the target (a long-lived signal would otherwise retain every element it ever saw); and each (target,type) Set is capped at 30 so a page re-binding in a loop cannot grow it unboundedly. Every patched function is passed through mask(fn, name, arity), which redefines .name, .length and .toString to return 'function NAME() { [native code] }' — enough to defeat the common `.toString().includes('[native code]')` probe, and the file states plainly that Function.prototype.toString.call() still sees through it. The registry's own two listeners are registered through origAdd so they never appear in the registry, and types starting with 'aiep:' are filtered out of the reply (reported back they would be attributed to the page as its 'real JavaScript', and the class-token match below is a substring test over words like 'list'/'data'/'name').
mechanisms.location: hook.js:1-90 (registry + mask), manifest.json content_scripts[0] {world:'MAIN', run_at:'document_start'}
mechanisms.chrome_apis_used: manifest content_scripts with world:'MAIN' at document_start
mechanisms.electron_equivalent: STRICTLY BETTER in Electron. A preload script with contextIsolation:false runs in the page's own world before any page script — that is the same thing without a manifest. Even better and isolation-safe: webContents.debugger + Page.addScriptToEvaluateOnNewDocument(source), which is guaranteed to run before every page script in EVERY frame and survives navigations, with no manifest and no world juggling. Node is available in preload, so the registry can stream straight to the main process.
mechanisms.port_notes: Port the three memory rules verbatim (once-skip, WeakRef signal cleanup, 30-per-type cap) — they are the difference between a registry and a leak. The mask() anti-detection can be DROPPED for our own generated projects (we are not hiding from ourselves) but should be kept for the 'import someone else's page' path. Because we own the mini-browser we can also install the hook via Page.addScriptToEvaluateOnNewDocument and get automatic re-injection on navigation, which the extension had to handle by hand.

mechanisms.name: hook.js — the registry query: subtree walk, delegation hoist, shadow piercing, source capture
mechanisms.problem: Answering 'what listens on this element' cheaply, across shadow roots, without freezing a delegation-heavy SPA.
mechanisms.how_it_works: The content script tags each element to be asked about with data-aiep-q="qN" and dispatches a CustomEvent('aiep:listeners:query', {detail: nonce}). The hook answers on 'aiep:listeners:reply' with a JSON STRING as detail (a structured detail does not survive the MAIN→isolated world boundary). Inside: delegated handlers on document/window/body/documentElement are collected ONCE for the whole query, not per element — rebuilding them per element turned a scan of a delegation-heavy SPA into a multi-second freeze. Tagged elements are found by a recursive sweep that re-runs querySelectorAll('[data-aiep-q]') inside every node's shadowRoot up to depth 6, because querySelectorAll stops at a shadow boundary and a component inside one reported no listeners and was skipped by the recorder. For each tagged element: itself plus up to 40 descendants; for each, every registry type is added to an events Set and up to 12 handlers pushed as {type, on:'self'|'descendant', source}; inline on* ATTRIBUTES are counted as listeners too ({on:'inline'}). Handler source is String(fn).slice(0,4000) memoised in a WeakMap. Delegated handlers are attributed to an element only by a labelled HEURISTIC: the element's class tokens (>=3 chars, identifier-shaped) appearing as substrings inside the handler's source, tagged {on:'delegated'}.
