subsystem: IDEAS.md — the 23-idea research corpus (E:\exten Picker\IDEAS.md, 570 lines, Arabic), cross-verified against the shipped v3.2.0 code (content.js 7300+ lines, hook.js, background.js, sidepanel.js)
summary: IDEAS.md is the output of a 21-agent / 670-web-search research run that survived 23 ideas past a 6.5 threshold on score = novelty*0.35 + impact*0.35 + feasibility*0.30. Its central thesis is that every competing tool assumes the unit of capture is THE PAGE, when the user actually wants A REUSABLE COMPONENT — and that "abstraction" is a word absent from every competitor's vocabulary. Verified against the shipped code: 5 ideas shipped substantially (#1 State Ghost, #2 ancestor context, #13 handler registry, #18 motion extraction, and an inverted #5), 5 shipped partially (#3, #9, #11, #15, #23), and 13 never shipped at all — including four (#7, #8, #14, #17) whose entire supporting apparatus exists in the author's throwaway `scratchpad/audit.js` CDP harness rather than in the product. For EXELMJ the load-bearing finding is that the *shipped* half is the CSS-cascade reader and the *unshipped* half is everything an Electron app can do trivially that a Chrome extension could not: real windows at arbitrary widths, a real filesystem, CDP, and Node.

mechanisms.name: #1 شبح الحالات — State Ghost (State Matrix) — score 8.7 (novelty 9 / impact 9 / feasibility 8) — SHIPPED, and shipped BEYOND its spec
mechanisms.problem: getComputedStyle only ever reports the instant you asked. A button's hover colour, a card's lift, a menu's open state are never 'applied' at copy time, so every tool on the market produces a visually-dead copy. The single most distinctive part of a design is exactly the part that is lost.
mechanisms.how_it_works: Read what COULD apply instead of what IS applied. (1) eachStyleRule walks every reachable stylesheet PER TREE SCOPE (document AND each shadow root, since a shadow sheet never crosses the boundary), descending @media/@supports/@layer, resolving CSS nesting (`&` -> `:is(parentSel)`, bare nested selector -> implicit descendant), synthesising an entry for CSSNestedDeclarations (Chrome 130+ rules that carry declarations but no selectorText — a walker keying on selectorText drops them silently), flagging @starting-style blocks, and walking adoptedStyleSheets LAST because they cascade last. (2) Each rule is filed into a per-scope index (WeakMap scope->rules) with a token set extracted from the selector (.class / #id / tag) and a boolean isState = ANY_STATE_RE.test(selectorText) || isStartingStyle. (3) ANY_STATE_RE matches :hover|:focus|:focus-visible|:focus-within|:active|:disabled|:checked|:visited|:invalid|:open|:popover-open, [data-state|data-open|data-expanded|...], [aria-expanded|selected|current|invalid|pressed|checked|hidden], [disabled], [open], .is-open|.is-active|..., and OPEN_CLASS_RE = /\.[a-zA-Z][\w-]*\.(?:open|opened|expanded|collapsed|shown|menu-open|nav-open|is-open)\b/ — a COMPOUNDED marker only. Bare `.open` and bare `.active` are deliberately excluded because half the web uses them for the current nav link, and moving those out of the resting rules leaves ordinary elements previewing unstyled. (4) statesFor(root) builds `have` = token set of the subtree (root + first 200 descendants) and skips any rule sharing no token — without this filter a Tailwind-sized sheet turns extraction into millions of matches() calls. (5) For each surviving state rule, split on commas (only some parts of a grouped selector carry the state), compute baseSelector(sel) by STRIPPING every marker ANY_STATE_RE recognises — the two regexes must stay in lockstep or a rule gets filed as a state and then fails the very match test that filing it there was meant to let it pass — then matchableSelector() removes the ::before/::after tail (matches('.btn::after') is always false, so those rules used to be discarded, taking the glows and overlays that ARE the design). (6) triggerSelector(sel, stateRe) splits on whitespace and cuts AFTER the first part carrying the state: in `.card:hover .title` the trigger is `.card` and the target is `.title`. The output is a TRIPLE — (what to touch, what kind of touch, what changes) — because the #1 reconstruction failure is hovering the card when the thing that changes is the heading inside it. (7) The delta: read each declared value against getComputedStyle(sample, pseudoOf(target)) and drop anything equal (so 'changes' means changed). Shorthands holding a custom property (`background: var(--brand)`) read back EMPTY on every longhand, so declarationsOf() falls back to recording the shorthand itself rather than copying var(--brand) into background-image, which would be invalid CSS. VERIFIED SHIPPED. The code also goes past the doc: componentStateRules() ships the author's VERBATIM declarations because the doc's property-whitelist summary can only carry what someone thought to list — a multi-step interaction (click, icon flies off, label swaps to 'Sent') came out as a colour change. mechanisms.name: #3 التمثيل الوسيط للمكوّن وطيّ التكرار — Component IR + Repetition Collapse — score 8.35 (7/10/8) — SHIPPED ONLY AS A DATA HARVESTER; the IR itself was never built
mechanisms.problem: A developer wants ready component code (React/Vue), not a giant file. Throwing a raw page at an LLM fails on size alone: a 200-row table eats the whole budget.
mechanisms.how_it_works: THE DESIGN (this is the part EXELMJ's builder should implement in full): before any AI, build a clean intermediate representation. Detect repeated SIBLING elements (same tag path + same class fingerprint), diff their contents, and promote whatever differs between them to DATA — so a 200-row table becomes one template + a 200-element data array. That alone is ~50x compression before the model sees anything, and critically it is not blind compression: template+data is EXACTLY the shape the developer wanted anyway, so the token-saving step and the output-quality step are the same step. Only then is a small, clean IR handed to a model to turn into component code. WHAT ACTUALLY SHIPPED: repetition detection exists in FOUR places and all four collapse to records, never to a template. (a) extractRepeats() — for each element with >=4 children, sig(n) = tagName + '|' + first 3 classes joined by '.'; require >=4 matching AND matching/total >= 0.7; prefer the DEEPEST such container (skip if the parent was already taken); per item pull innerText(300), first a[href] absolutised, first img.src, and first h1-h5/[class*=title]/[class*=name] as the title. (b) findBestRepeatContainer() — same signature, threshold 3, scored by same.length * (1 + count of ':' in the first child's innerText), i.e. it prefers containers whose children carry LABEL: VALUE lines. (c) cardToRecord() — the only 'differencing' that ships: split innerText into lines, match /^(.{1,50}?)\s*[:：]\s*(.+)$/ per line and use the left side as a COLUMN NAME and the right side as the value; the first unmatched line becomes 'العنوان'. This turns rendered government-portal cards into real columns with no JSON endpoint anywhere. (d) In the component scan, repetition is used only for DEDUP and RANKING: a two-tier signature — motionSignature(el) (concatenated animationName + transitionProperty+duration over the first 24 descendants, deliberately INERT on static pages) is the first key, and only once a group is seen holding >=3 DIFFERENT motions does it escalate to structureSignature(el) (child count + tag.class chain over 24 descendants, TEXT EXCLUDED ON PURPOSE because differing text is data). Measured: developer.mozilla.org grows 0%, a motion gallery goes from 7 cards to 144. There is NO template extraction, NO slot/hole discovery, NO IR type, and NO LLM-to-code call anywhere in the codebase.

mechanisms.name: #4 مُخرِج مضبوط على ميزانية النموذج — LLM-Budgeted Serializer — score 8.35 (8/9/8) — NOT SHIPPED for UI (a budgeted serializer exists, but only for source code review)
mechanisms.problem: 'Give this page to the AI' has no solution today: either a multi-megabyte file that blows the limit immediately, or plain text that loses all structure and design. Nothing in between.
mechanisms.how_it_works: THE DESIGN: a serializer whose objective is inverted from every other tool's. Images become short descriptions (dimensions + dominant colour + alt text) instead of their bytes; styles become REFERENCES to design tokens instead of declaration blocks; repeated regions fold to '×12'; there is an explicit budget switch (8k / 32k / 128k tokens) and a documented degradation ladder that tells the user what was dropped and why. The semantic backbone is the ACCESSIBILITY TREE, because it is the most accurate compact description of an interface and no capture tool emits one. The insight is that compressing for 'file size a browser opens' and compressing for 'tokens a model understands' are OPPOSITE objectives — Base64-inlining an image is excellent for the former and catastrophic for the latter. WHAT SHIPPED: not this. getCodeForReview(budget=60000) at content.js:4137-4189 is a real budgeted, prioritised slicer — but for the security tab's SOURCE CODE review, not the UI. It walks inline scripts and same-origin script files, prefers small non-vendor files ('smaller than vendor bundles, and small files fit the budget better'), skips minified vendor code as burning budget for no insight, and returns {chunks, bytes, budget}. The UI-side payload formatter (content.js:620-720) has json/html/markdown modes with no budget knob at all. getAccessibility() (content.js:464-483) is attribute scraping — role, all aria-*, alt, title — with a naive accessibleName = aria-label || alt || title || textContent.slice(0,80). It is not an accessibility TREE (no name computation algorithm, no implicit roles, no tree pruning). No image-to-description substitution exists; the clone-page path does the opposite and Base64-inlines images under a 25MB budget.

mechanisms.how_it_works: THE DESIGN: the user clicks what matters. Listen at CAPTURE phase on document, resolve the true event path (piercing closed components), snapshot world state before and after, diff: what changed in the tree, where focus went, and above all whether a new element appeared appended to the end of the body (a portal) or in the top layer — which is where every modern dialog and menu lives. Real user events are trusted; synthetic clicks are marked isTrusted:false and genuinely change page behaviour, so automated testing measures a different system than the real one. WHAT SHIPPED (content.js:5592-6320, the largest single subsystem in the file): the OPPOSITE — an automated 'live behavior recorder' that performs the interactions itself, because the doc's static-CSS motion path cannot capture spring engines that write style.transform 60x/sec. Its safety cage is the interesting artifact: (1) `click` is NEVER dispatched blindly — springs run on pointerdown/up, which is what gets sent instead. (2) clickUnsafe(el, behavior) runs over the WHOLE subtree (up to 60 nodes, because the event lands on whatever elementFromPoint returns, almost always a descendant, not the vetted root) and refuses if: el.closest('form'), any A[href], any submit/reset button, any inline on* attribute matching EFFECT_RE, DESTRUCTIVE_RE matching the label (delete|remove|buy|checkout|pay|submit|logout|... plus the Arabic احذف|شراء|ادفع|أرسل|تأكيد|خروج), OR — the strict part — if there are no READABLE non-delegated handlers at all ('no handler to read means nothing to clear it with'), OR if any readable handler SOURCE matches EFFECT_RE = /fetch\(|XMLHttpRequest|sendBeacon|window\.open|location\.(href|assign|replace)|location=|\.submit\(|\.click\(|history\.(pushState|replaceState)|localStorage|sessionStorage|indexedDB|document\.cookie|navigator\.clipboard/. (3) hook.js 'quiet mode' holds sendBeacon (returns true), window.open (returns null), history.pushState/replaceState, and MUTATING fetch/XHR (POST|PUT|PATCH|DELETE — GET/HEAD pass untouched, because silencing all requests breaks the page mid-session, a worse bug). Held fetches return a promise that NEVER settles so no error surfaces. Quiet mode SELF-EXPIRES after 8s in case the content script is torn down mid-recording. (4) A window guard preventDefaults untrusted events and stopImmediatePropagation()s any untrusted click the recorder did not aim (allowClickOn holds the single permitted target). (5) Escape is sent ONLY if overlayCount() (dialog[open], [role=dialog], [role=alertdialog], [aria-modal=true]) actually increased — firing it unconditionally closed dialogs the USER had open.

mechanisms.name: #6 استنتاج ارتباط البيانات بالواجهة — Data-Binding Inference — score 8.1 (novelty 10/10 — the highest novelty score in the file) — NOT SHIPPED (the capture half ships; the matching half does not exist)
mechanisms.problem: An extracted copy is full of hardcoded text and numbers with no meaning. Nobody knows which string came from a database and which is a design constant, so the copy is rigid and cannot be wired to real data.
mechanisms.how_it_works: THE DESIGN: capture the data that reached the page (network responses AND — the biggest and most-forgotten case — payloads injected inline at first load by SSR frameworks), then match every visible string against its location inside that data. The hard part is that a number appears FORMATTED ('١٢٬٥٠٠ ر.س'), never raw, so invert the formatting: strip symbols, coerce to number, index by the numeric value, then try the standard format recipes against only the handful of candidates — turning a minutes-long operation into milliseconds. The strongest evidence is ORDINAL alignment: if list item #3 matches data record #3 across three or more items, that is near-proof. The NEGATIVE result is equally valuable: 'these four words matched nothing' means they are design constants, which a rebuilder needs as much as the positive result. WHAT SHIPPED: only the capture. background.js NET_INTERCEPTOR is injected into the MAIN world on demand (chrome.scripting.executeScript with world:'MAIN'), patches window.fetch and XMLHttpRequest.open/send, filters on content-type /json|text\/csv|application\/xml|text\/xml|graphql/i OR a .json URL, caps bodies at 3MB, and postMessage's each record to the content script, which keeps a 300-entry ring buffer. summariseJson() then does a depth<=4 search for the first array of objects and reports {records: n, fields: first 15 keys}. That is where it stops — the buffer is listed in a Data tab and can be downloaded. There is NO text-to-payload matching, NO format inversion, NO ordinal alignment, and NO SSR inline-payload harvesting (__NEXT_DATA__ / __NUXT__ appear zero times).

mechanisms.name: #7 مواصفة قبول قابلة للتنفيذ ومولّد القواعد الثابتة — Executable Acceptance Spec + Invariant Generator — score 8.1 (9/9/6) — NOT SHIPPED in the product; the author built the diagnosis half as a throwaway CDP harness and left it in scratchpad
mechanisms.problem: The user extracts a component, rebuilds it with AI, and has no way to know whether the result is correct. The defect surfaces hours later, after manual editing.
mechanisms.how_it_works: THE DESIGN, in two halves. HALF ONE — generate invariants AUTOMATICALLY (never by hand) from measurements already taken: equal gaps between siblings => a `gap` rule; a present `margin-left:auto` => 'the last item right-aligns'; a stable width/height ratio => an aspect-ratio rule; a text/background colour pair => a contrast rule. The economics argument is the important one: hand-written checklists never generalise, whereas a few hundred lines of generator scales to any component automatically. HALF TWO — actually RUN the rebuilt code in an isolated page and verify NODE BY NODE, then REPLAY the user's recorded interactions against the new copy. The doc calls verification 'the real moat: not extraction, proof.' WHAT SHIPPED: the sandbox host, and nothing else. sidepanel.js previewDoc/mountPreview build an <iframe sandbox="" srcdoc=...> — no same-origin, no scripts, so the page's CSS renders and nothing runs — with the #2 wrapper chain and a transform:scale fit, mounted lazily via IntersectionObserver with a 150px rootMargin. There is no invariant generator and no verification pass in the product. HOWEVER, Session-Notes records that the author built exactly the missing machinery OUTSIDE the extension: scratchpad/audit.js + audit-lib.js extract the real content.js functions, run them in Chrome over CDP, build each card's preview, and compare it against the live card on three fingerprints — motion, paint, and size — yielding verdicts PASS / SIZE-DIFF / PAINT-DIFF / MOTION-DIFF. Measured progression across sessions: 111 PASS -> 114 -> 120 of 144, MOTION-DIFF 1 -> 0, PAINT-DIFF 11 -> 8 -> 1. That harness found and fixed four real product bugs (grouped-selector truncation, shorthand-with-var serialisation, :has() inversion, keyframe vars).

mechanisms.name: #8 طبقة إصلاح المظهر وتشخيص انحراف التخطيط — Paint-Only Repair Layer + Layout Divergence Diagnosis — score 8.0 (8/8/8) — NOT SHIPPED as a layer; the paint/layout SPLIT is nonetheless the organising principle of the author's audit tool
mechanisms.problem: The copy comes out close but not identical; the user sees the difference and knows neither its cause nor its location.
mechanisms.how_it_works: THE DESIGN: compare every element in the copy to its counterpart in the original and PARTITION the properties into two classes with opposite treatment. PAINT properties (color, background, box-shadow, border, font) may be pinned directly and safely, because they do not affect size or position — and this is where most real failures actually live. LAYOUT properties (width, height, margins) are FORBIDDEN from being pinned, because pixel-pinning makes the result look identical while having killed the design's responsiveness. Any layout divergence is instead REPORTED as a diagnosis: 'this element's width differs by 40px because its parent in the original is a grid column that was not captured.' The doc is explicit that the original version of this idea claimed to 'always converge' and in fact converged by destroying the product and reporting success; the split between what-is-repaired and what-is-diagnosed 'is what turns the tool from a confident liar into an honest assistant', and the diagnosis is more useful to the user than the silent repair. WHAT SHIPPED: no repair layer, no diagnosis surface in the product. But the audit harness's verdict vocabulary IS this partition — PAINT-DIFF versus SIZE-DIFF are separate verdicts, and the author's own analysis of the residual 21-23 SIZE-DIFFs is precisely the doc's diagnosis form: 'not defects — the gallery's CSS grid stretches every card in a row to the tallest; confirmed, all of them have parentDisplay===grid.'

mechanisms.electron_equivalent: Offscreen document -> a hidden BrowserWindow (show:false) or an offscreen WebContentsView, both of which have REAL dimensions (the failure mode #17 warns about). Property comparison via CDP CSS.getComputedStyleForNode on both sides, or executeJavaScript in each.
mechanisms.port_notes: Port the PARTITION, which is the whole idea, and enforce it in the type system: `type PaintProp = ...` may be auto-pinned, `type LayoutProp = ...` may only produce a Diagnosis object. mechanisms.name: #9 إحصاء رموز التصميم واستخراج السلالم — Design Token Census & Scale Archaeology — score 7.95 (6/9/9, the highest feasibility in tier one) — SHIPPED, but the census only; every clustering step in the spec is missing
mechanisms.problem: What people actually mean by 'copy this site' is: give me the type scale, the spacing rhythm, the colour palette, the radii, the shadows, the breakpoints. What they get is a huge file and then they eyedrop colours one at a time.
mechanisms.how_it_works: THE DESIGN: count the values actually USED across every element, weight by frequency, then cluster with INTELLIGENT TOLERANCE — spacing snapped to the nearest 4px, colours merged by a PERCEPTUAL colour-difference metric, font sizes searched for a regular GEOMETRIC ratio. Then compare the result against the variables the site itself declares: sites with a real design system hand you the token NAMES for free, and only the remainder needs naming — by one small bounded LLM call over ~40 values. Output as CSS variables, a Tailwind config, or JSON. The doc calls the AI call here 'safe and cheap because it only names numbers and produces no code — it cannot hallucinate anything dangerous', and rates this the best value-to-effort ratio in the entire list. WHAT SHIPPED: extractStyles() walks up to 5000 elements (deepAll, i.e. piercing shadow roots), skips display:none/visibility:hidden, and tallies — colors keyed by hex with a usage set {text, background, border}; fonts keyed by first family with size and weight SETS plus the full stack; fontSizes; gradients (backgroundImage containing 'gradient', first 400 chars); shadows (first 200 chars); radii (Math.round, with >=500 collapsed to the sentinel 9999 meaning 'full'); spacings from paddingTop/paddingBottom/marginTop/gap where 0 < n <= 160. Everything is sorted by count and truncated (30 colours, 8 fonts, 5 gradients, 6 shadows, 8 radii, 10 spacings, 8 type sizes). Then sidepanel.js buildDesignSystem() assigns ROLES: pickRoles() converts to HSL, calls a colour neutral if s<0.14 || l<0.07 || l>0.96, takes the most-used vivid colour as primary, the first vivid colour >60deg away in hue as accent, the first other vivid colour <=60deg away as secondary, and a mid-lightness neutral; buildRamp() then SYNTHESISES a 50-950 ramp by holding H and S and substituting fixed lightness stops. Labels are hardcoded (xs/sm/base/lg/xl/2xl/3xl/4xl; sm/md/lg/xl/2xl for radii; 1-8 for spacing). Exports: CSS custom properties, `tailwind.config.js`, and W3C Design Tokens JSON ({$type:'color', $value:...}). MISSING vs spec: no 4px snapping (spacing is Math.round to 1px, so 15px and 16px stay separate tokens), no perceptual colour merge (exact hex equality only, so #4f46e5 and #4f46e6 are two tokens), no geometric-ratio detection (typeScale is literally the top 8 sizes by frequency, sorted ascending), NO reading of the site's own declared custom properties for names, and no LLM naming call.

mechanisms.name: #10 تفريع الثيم — إنتاج النسخة الداكنة — Theme Fork (Dark Mode Artifact) — score 7.7 (8/8/7) — NOT SHIPPED (zero occurrences of prefers-color-scheme or color-scheme in the entire codebase)
mechanisms.problem: The user captures a site in light mode and gets light mode only, even though the site's own files contain a complete dark theme.
mechanisms.how_it_works: THE DESIGN: the browser hands you the dark-mode rules even while you are in light mode — they are parsed, present and readable, merely not active. So run a SECOND, ANALYTICAL CASCADE that computes how each element WOULD look under dark mode, and emit both variants. Two make-or-break details the doc calls out by name: (1) dark mode in today's most popular CSS framework is NOT a media query but a CLASS on the root written in a convoluted selector form, so the rule parser must understand that form or the feature fails SILENTLY on the most common case of all; (2) copy the `color-scheme` property onto the wrapper — that is what makes scrollbars, form fields and native dropdowns paint correctly, and it is the detail everyone hand-rolling dark mode gets wrong. Also: extract the toggle button ONLY when there is confirmed evidence linking localStorage to the class that is actually present, 'because a dead button is worse than no button.' WHAT SHIPPED: nothing. `prefers-color-scheme`, `color-scheme`, `@media (prefers` all appear 0 times. The word `dark` appears 4 times in content.js and every occurrence is a filter regex (ancestorContext's /dark|light|theme|rtl|ltr|mode/i ancestor-class filter, and semanticClasses' utility-variant blacklist which drops `dark:` prefixed classes). The SUBSTRATE is fully built though: ruleIndex already stores `media` per rule and eachStyleRule already carries the condition text down through nested @media/@supports/@layer, so the analytical second cascade has everything it needs.

The analytical path remains valuable for producing a STATIC dark artifact without a live page.
mechanisms.port_notes: Implement the empirical path first (Emulation.setEmulatedMedia + re-measure) because Electron makes it nearly free, and keep the analytical path for offline artifacts. Do NOT skip the two details the doc flags: parse the class-based dark selector form, and carry `color-scheme` through — both are silent-failure sources. mechanisms.name: #11 رفع المتغيّرات وبناء شجرة نطاقاتها — Var Lift, Scoped Custom Property Tree — score 7.65 (8/7/8) — PARTIALLY SHIPPED: the lifting works and the silent-failure guard works; the scope TREE does not exist

mechanisms.name: #12 المقارنة الدلالية بين التقاطين — Semantic Capture Diff — score 7.65 (8/7/8) — NOT SHIPPED (no IndexedDB, no hashing, no capture store)
mechanisms.problem: The user wants to know what CHANGED on a competitor's page or in their own product between two captures, and gets two enormous files that cannot be compared at all.
mechanisms.how_it_works: THE DESIGN: hash every subtree of the page's tree, and SEPARATELY hash its styling, and store both locally. On the next capture, compare tree-to-tree hash by hash to locate differences exactly. Because the STRUCTURE hash is independent of the STYLE hash, you can distinguish 'the content changed' from 'the design changed' — which is the distinction that actually matters for price monitoring, design-system drift, and visual regressions. The doc notes existing tools diff at the file/byte level and deliberately AVOID reloading, i.e. exactly backwards. The key line: separating structure hash from style hash turns 'something changed' into an actionable answer — did the competitor change their price, or their brand identity? WHAT SHIPPED: nothing. `indexedDB` occurs exactly once in content.js and it is inside the EFFECT_RE safety regex. There is no hash function beyond crc32 (used only for the ZIP central directory). There IS a local component LIBRARY (sidepanel.js LIB_KEY='uiLibrary' in chrome.storage.local with a libId() identity built from name+kind+size+text lengths), but it stores, it does not diff. Note: structureSignature()/motionSignature() (content.js:5439-5470) are exactly the right shape of primitive for this and were built for dedup instead.

mechanisms.name: #13 سجل معالجات الأحداث وحلّ التفويض — Handler Registry + Delegation Resolution — score 7.4 (8/8/6) — SHIPPED (registry + delegation heuristic); the definitive dispatch test and the primitive-action classifier did NOT ship
mechanisms.problem: A copied component does nothing when clicked, because the code responsible for its behaviour is never captured. And a naive inventory reports 'this button has no listeners' in ~100% of cases, because modern frameworks attach everything to the app root.
mechanisms.how_it_works: WHAT SHIPPED (hook.js in full, 12KB, world:'MAIN' at document_start so it runs before ANY page script): EventTarget.prototype.addEventListener is replaced by a patched version that files (this, type, fn) into a WeakMap target -> Map(type -> Set(fn)) before delegating to the original. Careful details: `once` listeners are SKIPPED outright, because the browser removes them without ever calling removeEventListener, so storing them pins dead closures for the page's life and the 30-per-type cap then starts rejecting LIVE ones; an AbortSignal gets an abort listener (registered through the ORIGINAL addEventListener, or it would file itself in the registry it is meant to clean) holding a WeakRef to the target, because a long-lived signal would otherwise retain every element it ever saw. The patch masks itself: name, length and a toString returning 'function addEventListener() { [native code] }' — the file states plainly that Function.prototype.toString.call() still sees through it rather than papering over it. QUERY PATH: the content script tags elements with data-aiep-q and fires a CustomEvent with a nonce; hook.js sweeps the document AND recursively every shadowRoot to depth 6 (querySelectorAll stops at shadow boundaries, so components inside one reported zero listeners and were skipped entirely), collects per-element listeners over the element + up to 40 descendants, adds inline on* attributes as listeners, and replies with a JSON STRING inside a CustomEvent (a structured detail does not survive the MAIN->isolated boundary). DELEGATION: handlers on document/window/body/documentElement are collected ONCE per query, not per element — rebuilding them per element turned a scan of a delegation-heavy SPA into a multi-second freeze — and attributed to an element by the only usable link available: whether the element's class tokens (>=3 chars, identifier-shaped) appear as SUBSTRINGS in the handler's source. The file labels this a heuristic. NOT SHIPPED: the doc's definitive test — dispatch a synthetic event and WRAP each handler to see which one actually ran — and the primitive-action classifier (toggle class / flip aria attribute / preventDefault / submit) that emits working code. Instead the handler SOURCES ship verbatim as an inert reference block. The doc's best insight survives implicitly though: variable names are mangled by bundlers but PROPERTY names and string constants like `classList` and `aria-expanded` CANNOT be mangled — and content.js:5668 EFFECT_RE is exactly that kind of source-string classifier, repurposed as a SAFETY gate rather than a code generator.

mechanisms.name: #14 المسح التجريبي لنقاط الكسر والحاويات — Empirical Breakpoint & Container Sweep — score 7.35 (8/7/7) — NOT SHIPPED, and the shipped preview actively suffers from its absence
mechanisms.problem: A copied component looks right on one screen and collapses on mobile, and the user knows neither at what width it breaks nor why.
mechanisms.how_it_works: THE DESIGN — and this is the technical heart of deliverable (d): render the component at a LADDER of widths inside an isolated frame, take a LAYOUT FINGERPRINT at each width, then BINARY-SEARCH for the real transition points. The make-or-break condition, stated as an absolute: the fingerprint must be composed of DISCRETE values only — number of columns, NOT column width; flex direction; number of text LINES; whether an element is visible at all. If you fingerprint pixel values they change at every step and you 'find' a breakpoint at nearly every width, which is pure noise. Sweep CONTAINER width on an axis SEPARATE from viewport width, because they are genuinely different axes (a component in a sidebar and the same component in a main column see different container widths at the same viewport width). Add a root-font-size sweep for accessibility. The doc's sharpest point: the DECLARED breakpoints are not the valuable output — those are written in the file and can simply be read. The valuable output is the EMERGENT breakpoints nobody intended: the width where a label wraps to two lines and overflows its box. Those are the failures real users see and that no code reader can find. WHAT SHIPPED: nothing. `matchMedia`, `breakpoint`, `@container`, `containerType`, `ResizeObserver` all appear 0 times. Worse — and this is the strongest possible argument for building (d) — the shipped preview is an iframe roughly 150px wide, so EVERY mobile media query fires inside it, and the author flagged this in Session-Notes as a live hazard he chose not to fix: 'the preview is a frame about 150px wide, so all the mobile media queries run inside it. On kinetics it only hides two elements, but it is a potential source of failures on other sites — UNADDRESSED.' The 40% viewport-area penalty in paintScore has the same disease: viewArea is computed from window.innerWidth*innerHeight, which CHANGES when the side panel opens, so gallery cards were scored as page furniture and dropped, and the fix (repeatedItem exemption) is a workaround for not being able to control the viewport.

mechanisms.name: #15 بصمة الأيقونات والأصول — Icon & Asset Fingerprinting — score 7.3 (6/8/8) — PARTIALLY SHIPPED: the icon-font path is implemented as RENDERING, not as NAMING; no library matching at all
mechanisms.problem: Icons are captured as long geometric path strings that consume enormous space and mean nothing, when what is needed is the NAME: 'arrow-right', 'trash'.
mechanisms.how_it_works: THE DESIGN: reduce the icon's shape to a compact fingerprint and match it against well-known icon libraries to recover its name instead of its shape. Cover all FOUR real kinds, not one: inline-drawn SVG, references into a sprite sheet, CSS mask declarations, and ICON FONTS. The doc's counter-intuitive punchline: the EASIEST case (icon fonts) is also 100% the most ACCURATE, because each icon is a character with a fixed codepoint that maps directly to a name via a small lookup table with zero guessing, whereas complex shape matching only ever yields a guess. Normally the cheapest method is the weakest; here it is the reverse, which fixes the build order — start with the easiest and most exact. Pixel analysis of images must go through a background fetch or the browser taints the canvas. Fallback is a crop out of a captureVisibleTab screenshot, with the picker's own shadow-DOM UI hidden for 60ms first and tainted-canvas failures skipped silently. mechanisms.name: #16 نقطة تعقيم واحدة للبيانات الحسّاسة — Unified Redaction Choke Point — score 7.3 (6/8/8) — NOT SHIPPED as a choke point; redaction exists in two unrelated places with two unrelated policies

mechanisms.how_it_works: THE DESIGN: ONE redaction point every output passes through, with a policy that varies by DESTINATION. Values visible on screen are replaced by realistic text OF THE SAME LENGTH (a name for a name) so layout does not shift and measurements stay valid. Values inside data payloads are replaced by STABLE PSEUDONYMS that preserve TYPE rather than length, because what the model needs is the SHAPE of the data, not its content. Any high-entropy string, or one starting with a known key prefix, is blanked immediately — and anything that cannot be classified is ALSO blanked, so the error always leans toward safety. The doc's justification for making it a single mandatory gate rather than a per-feature responsibility: 'this is the only part of the whole product where a mistake is a security incident rather than a poor output — one feature forgetting to redact is enough to destroy trust in the entire product.' (1) The security scanner has maskMatch(text, severity, ruleId, mask) and maskContext(text), gated on an OPT-IN `mask` flag (default false) with an ALWAYS_MASK set plus automatic masking for critical/high severity — but it only redacts the scanner's own finding excerpts, not any other output. (2) The dialect-corpus harvester has its own independent PII cleaner. Put the component in an isolated capsule, delete one rule or one wrapper, re-measure, and if nothing changed visually, delete it permanently. THREE conditions without which it cannot work: (1) the capsule must have REAL DIMENSIONS, or every measurement is zero and every deletion 'succeeds'; (2) the site's fonts must actually LOAD, or every text shifts and every measurement fails; (3) a PRE-FLIGHT SAFETY GATE must confirm the capsule matches the live page BEFORE any deletion starts, because deleting on top of a skewed baseline produces confident garbage. mechanisms.name: #18 استخراج الحركة — Motion Extraction (Static + WAAPI + Mutation Ledger) — score 7.0 (7/7/7) — SHIPPED, and the third path was replaced by something stronger than the spec
mechanisms.problem: The copy comes out completely static: no fade-in, no transitions, no entrance motion — while motion is a fundamental part of how a site feels.
mechanisms.how_it_works: THE DESIGN: three paths by motion SOURCE. (a) Motion written in stylesheets is read STATICALLY, for free, with no need to play it — the doc explicitly corrects an earlier version of the idea that wanted to trigger animations to capture them. (b) Transitions and modern scripted animations are read from the browser's animation API. (c) Popular libraries that draw motion frame-by-frame by WRITING STYLES DIRECTLY never appear in any animation API at all, so they are caught with a bounded time-ordered LEDGER of style changes as they happen. Validation is by sampling three points and comparing against the expected curve rather than blind trust. The doc's sharpest correction: the common claim that 'scrubbing the timeline recovers every animation' is false, because the world's most popular motion library creates no animation object at all. WHAT SHIPPED: path (a) fully — motionFor(root) collects transitions and animations off the root plus 60 descendants, lifts the @keyframes TEXT out of the CSSOM, splits shorthand lists with splitTopLevel() (which respects nesting so cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1) counts as ONE value, not four), extracts animation names with ANIM_KEYWORD_RE (skip infinite/normal/alternate/forwards/ease/linear/..., skip anything matching /^-?[\d.]+m?s$/ or a bare number, skip cubic-bezier(/steps(/linear( — the first surviving token is the name), and stateKeyframesFor() collects the keyframes a STATE reaches for, since a wave a button plays on hover never runs at rest and nothing else would find it. Path (b) is NOT used — getAnimations() appears 0 times in shipped code (it is used only in the scratchpad audit harness, to FREEZE animations). Path (c) was replaced by direct sampling: samplePhase drives the interaction and reads getComputedStyle across 26 RECORD_PROPS (including stroke-dashoffset/stroke-dasharray/stroke/fill/stroke-width, without which SVG progress rings read as 'nothing moved') on every rAF frame, then changedSeries() drops properties with <2 distinct values, drops NUMERIC_PROPS whose total range is <=1px (sub-pixel jitter is not motion), collapses consecutive duplicates, and decimates to 26 keyframes; phaseToBlocks() converts times to percentages against effDur = clamp(lastChangeTime + 60ms, 200, window) — NOT the full window, because a spring settling at 400ms of a 1200ms window was being stretched across the whole window and, since CSS synthesises the missing 100% frame from the resting style, the motion then ran BACKWARDS to base and `both` fill held it there, so the hover visibly undid itself while still hovered — and pins a 100% stop at the settled values. Nodes the stylesheet ALREADY animates are skipped (that is transcription, not capture, and re-emitting it fights the author's own keyframes). cssCoveredProps() suppresses any recorded property the author's own rule already covers, matched through COVER_ALIASES (comparing first-hyphen-segments instead let border-color cover border-radius and transform-origin cover transform, deleting real motion). resolvesInHtml() verifies each :nth-child binding against the ACTUALLY EXPORTED markup, because the page can inject a ripple span mid-press that the snapshot does not have. MEASURED on kinetics.colorion.co: 6 of 80 components record exportable motion; 77 carry real listener metadata.

mechanisms.name: #19 إرجاع المكوّن إلى أصله البرمجي — Component Repatriation (Framework Props Recovery) — score 7.0 (7/7/7) — NOT SHIPPED (zero framework probes, zero source-map handling)
mechanisms.problem: The extractor gets the rendered HTML, not the component that produced it — losing the component's NAME, its BOUNDARY, and the PROPS it accepts, which are the substance of any rebuild.
mechanisms.how_it_works: THE DESIGN, and the value is in how the expectation is calibrated: frameworks leave traces in the page that link each DOM element back to the component that created it and to the props passed to it. Read those traces and extract COMPONENT BOUNDARY + PROP SIGNATURE — and treat THAT as the primary deliverable, because it is available in real production builds. Recovering original source via source maps is treated as a RARE BONUS, never a promise, because most sites do not publish them and even when published they may not contain source text. But even the FILE NAMES alone reveal the framework, the project organisation, and the team's conventions. The doc's framing: 'the intelligence here is lowering the expectation to the right place — instead of betting on a rare path that gives everything, bet on a reliable path that gives the most important thing. Component boundary and prop signature reframe the whole task even when source recovery fails completely.' The doc's exclusions section additionally lists 'source recovery as a primary promise' among the things deliberately discarded, noting the browser already offers it in two clicks. WHAT SHIPPED: nothing. __reactFiber / __reactProps / __vue / __svelte / _x_dataStack / sourceMappingURL all appear ZERO times across all four JS files. componentName() (content.js:5347-5390) is the shipped substitute and it is pure text heuristics: aria-label, then innerText/textContent if <=40 chars (with unspaceLetters() to rejoin per-letter-animated text that reads back as 'S e n d  M e s s a g e'), then a PRIORITY-ORDERED list of selectors ['[class*="name" i]', 'h1..h6', '[class*="title" i]', 'figcaption'] — ordered because a single comma-joined selector cannot express priority, querySelector returns first-in-DOM-order, and a demo's inner .title was beating the card's own .name.

mechanisms.name: #20 بصمة التمرير — Scrollprint (Scroll Archetype Classifier) — score 6.75 (novelty 9, feasibility 5) — NOT SHIPPED (no IntersectionObserver, no parallax classifier, no scroll-position sampling)
mechanisms.problem: Modern sites are built around scrolling — elements revealing progressively, backgrounds moving at different rates, bars sticking — and none of it exists at the moment of capture, so the copy loses all of it.
mechanisms.how_it_works: THE DESIGN: CLASSIFY rather than RECORD. Instead of storing forty snapshots per element (an output nobody uses), recognise known archetypes and emit a compact description — 'parallax, factor 0.35' — four lines that work with any content length. Reuse the page's OWN registered IntersectionObservers to read exact reveal thresholds instead of guessing them, and fall back to expensive scanning only for elements with no observer. Mandatory safety gate: if the document height CHANGES during the sweep (infinite scroll), STOP and declare the analysis unavailable, because a silently wrong output is worse than no output. The doc notes this is the only feature that cannot be isolated — it must run on the user's real page — which is why it sits in tier three behind explicit consent. WHAT SHIPPED: nothing of the classifier. materializeLazyContent(budgetMs=12000) does scroll the page, but only to force lazy content to mount: it returns immediately if scrollHeight <= innerHeight*1.5, steps by max(400, innerHeight*0.9) with a 45ms settle per stop, is TIME-BOXED rather than run to the end (a heavy showcase spends close to a second per screen mounting, so an unbounded sweep of a long page hangs for minutes), reports progress, restores the original scrollY, waits 250ms for the last mounts to settle, and returns {truncated} so the caller knows the sweep was cut. Measured impact: on uiverse.io, 1 mounted component becomes 34. Note it does NOT implement the doc's height-change safety gate.

mechanisms.name: #21 التوأم القياسي للخطوط — Metric Twin (Font Fallback Synthesis) — score 6.65 (6/7/7) — NOT SHIPPED (no size-adjust / ascent-override synthesis anywhere)
mechanisms.problem: The extracted copy cannot use the site's original fonts (licensing and size), so every text width changes, alignment collapses, and boxes jump.
mechanisms.how_it_works: THE DESIGN: measure the ORIGINAL font as it is actually rendered on the page, then generate a system-font substitute tuned with correction factors (size-adjust / ascent-override / descent-override / line-gap-override) so its advance widths and line heights nearly match — preserving layout without shipping a single font file. Two precise conditions: (1) the measurement MUST include letter-spacing or the match fails on every real site; (2) a single LINE may be rendered by THREE different fonts (Latin + Arabic + emoji), so measurement must be PER-CHARACTER, not per-sentence, or you are comparing two different things. The doc singles out the payoff: existing tools rely on a precomputed metrics database and therefore fail on an unknown font, a variable font, or mixed-language text; live measurement of the font AS DRAWN removes that limit entirely, 'and this matters a great deal for Arabic content specifically.' WHAT SHIPPED: nothing. size-adjust / ascent-override appear 0 times. Font data collected is only family + the SET of sizes + the SET of weights + the full stack (extractStyles:1092-1100), and @font-face src URLs are harvested for download by the asset excavator. canvas measureText() is used exactly once, in renderGlyph, and only to detect ligature substitution. Notably content.js:1048 already normalises letterSpacing ('normal' -> '0px') in the WCAG contrast helper — the measurement the doc says is mandatory is one line away and unused.

mechanisms.name: #22 الربط المرقّم بين الصورة والنص — Set-of-Mark Binding — score 6.6 (novelty 4 — the lowest in the file / impact 8 / feasibility 8) — NOT SHIPPED (screenshots exist; numbering does not)
mechanisms.problem: When a model is given both a screenshot and a textual description of a page, it cannot confidently connect them: which box in the image is which element in the text?
mechanisms.how_it_works: THE DESIGN: overlay NUMBERS on the elements in the screenshot, and give the SAME elements the SAME numbers in the textual representation — so the two contexts become one context. The model can then say 'element 14', and you can translate that back to a LIVE element on the page and verify it. Just a clean shot plus a numbered shot; no complex image pyramid. The doc is unusually honest about this one: the technique is known in browser-agent research and MUST NOT be marketed as an innovation; the value is not the numbering itself but that the number is BIDIRECTIONAL — it goes from image to text, and comes BACK from the model's words to a real element that can be measured. That is what turns a description into something verifiable. WHAT SHIPPED: nothing. chrome.tabs.captureVisibleTab exists (background.js CAPTURE_TAB) and is used in three places — the colour-picker sampler, the element-screenshot crop, and the icon-crop fallback — but never for numbered overlays, and no IR ids exist to number (see #3).

mechanisms.name: #23 إزالة تكرار الأصول بالمحتوى لا بالرابط — Content-Addressed Asset Deduplication — score 6.5 (novelty 4 / impact 6 / feasibility 10 — the highest feasibility, and the lowest-ranked survivor) — PARTIALLY SHIPPED: URL-keyed dedup with two content-keyed exceptions

mechanisms.how_it_works: THE DESIGN: hash each asset's CONTENT (not its URL), keep a content-addressed store so each unique payload is stored once and referenced from everywhere, and lift CSS shared across multiple components into a single definition. The doc's own framing: not an innovation, but the cheapest and most certain item on the list — a documented flaw in the market-leading tool, fixable in a few dozen lines with no permissions and no risk. 'A guaranteed win you can build in a day.' WHAT SHIPPED: dedup is URL-keyed — a `seen` Set of absolute URLs guards every route() call in the asset excavator. TWO content-keyed exceptions exist: inline SVG is deduped on its normalised markup (dedupKey = markup.replace(/\s+/g,' ').trim(), tracked in markupSeen), and data: URLs are deduped on the URL string itself, which for a data URL IS the content. Named icons dedup globally while anonymous ones dedup by size+position. No hashing: crc32 exists (content.js:1871) but only to build the ZIP central directory. No shared-CSS lifting — componentCss re-emits each component's full rule set independently, and the scan explicitly ships each component's stylesheet WITH it, reasoning that 'the gallery renders every preview live, and fetching CSS per card would mean 40 round-trips.'

mechanisms.electron_equivalent: A real filesystem. Node crypto.createHash('sha256') instead of SubtleCrypto, and a plain content-addressed directory (objects/ab/cdef…) in app.getPath('userData'). This also removes the extension's serialised-write-chain workaround in background.js corpusAppend, which existed only because two tabs writing chrome.storage.local simultaneously clobber each other.
mechanisms.port_notes: Trivial in Electron and worth doing early because everything else (#12's capture store, #7's verification snapshots, #15's icon cache, #21's font cache) wants the same store. Note the shipped code already proves the value of content-keying for the one case where it was cheap (inline SVG markup) — generalising it is the whole task.

gotchas: THE AUTHOR'S OWN BUILD RECOMMENDATION (IDEAS.md:22-26), verbatim in substance: start with #2 (Element-Scoped Extraction, ranked SECOND at 8.4) BEFORE #1 (State Ghost, ranked FIRST at 8.7). The argument is dependency, not score: without reconstituting the ancestor environment (layout mode, variables, ancestor classes, containers) EVERY other feature is built on a skewed foundation, and everything above it comes out precise in form and wrong in result. #1 goes immediately after, IN THE SAME FIRST RELEASE, because it is the highest PERCEIVED value at the lowest technical cost — zero permissions, zero modification of the user's page — and it delivers something no competitor has today (the hover shape of a button, the popup, the second tab). The clincher: BOTH SHARE THE SAME ENGINE UNDERNEATH (stylesheet rule reader + cascade resolver + selector analyser), so building one builds half of the other for free. The proposed v1 is exactly four features: #2 + #1 + #9 (token census) + #8 (appearance repair) — all four with no alarming permission, and the set already includes the verification tool that differentiates the product from the market. FOR EXELMJ THE SAME DEPENDENCY ARGUMENT HOLDS, WITH ONE ADDITION: build #3's IR alongside #2, not after it, because in our case the extraction target is not a clipboard payload but the builder's document model — and an IR retrofitted onto an extractor is the same 'skewed foundation' mistake one level up.

DEAD ON ARRIVAL IN ELECTRON — port nothing: (a) the manifest-sandbox / offscreen-document requirement that dominates #7 and #17 and constrains #8, #11, #14, #21 — MV3 forbids running generated code in an extension page, which is why #7 scored only 6 on feasibility; in Electron a real BrowserWindow with contextIsolation runs anything. (b) chrome.dom.openOrClosedShadowRoot (content.js:1211-1215), an extension-only closed-shadow-root reader with no permission cost and NO Electron equivalent — replace with CDP DOM.getDocument({pierce:true}). (c) The whole MAIN-world/isolated-world bridge: hook.js's CustomEvent + JSON-string + nonce + 500ms-timeout protocol (hook.js:172-260, content.js:6180-6202) exists ONLY because a content script cannot share objects with the page — a preload with contextBridge deletes it. (d) The 'arm + reload' permission tier the doc builds a whole product strategy around (Strategic Theme #5, and the gating on #6, #13, #18, #20) — in Electron a preload always runs at document_start, so there is nothing to arm and no reload to ask for. (e) chrome.tabs.captureVisibleTab's visible-viewport-only limitation, which forced the in-view filter in captureIconCrops and the 60ms self-hide dance. (f) chrome.storage.local's 10MB pressure, which made sidepanel.js strip the recorded motion sample series before persisting, and forced background.js's serialised write chain against concurrent tabs. (g) The extension's inability to control viewport size, which produced the two ugliest scars in the code: the 150px-wide preview iframe where every mobile media query fires (flagged by the author as unaddressed), and paintScore's viewArea penalty computed from a window that shrinks when the side panel opens — a threshold the author himself calls 'inherently unstable'.

EASIER OR NEWLY POSSIBLE IN ELECTRON — where the port BUYS capability rather than just preserving it: #14 (empirical breakpoint sweep) goes from 'feasibility 7, deferred to tier two, never built' to nearly free — WebContentsView.setBounds and CDP Emulation.setDeviceMetricsOverride give a REAL viewport at any width, which is simultaneously deliverable (d)'s desktop/tablet/mobile switcher and the sweep's driver. #7 (acceptance spec) and #17 (ablation capsule) lose their single blocking constraint (nowhere to run generated code) and #17 loses all three of its stated preconditions (real dimensions -> setBounds; fonts actually loaded -> Node fetch + disk cache; pre-flight equality gate -> #7). #10 (theme fork) becomes empirical rather than analytical via nativeTheme.themeSource and Emulation.setEmulatedMedia — you can just RENDER it dark and measure. #1's cross-origin stylesheet problem — the extension's single largest SILENT failure, where .cssRules throws SecurityError and the rules are dropped with no signal — disappears because the main process can fetch and parse any sheet with Node. #6 (data-binding) gains CDP Network.getResponseBody, which sees bodies the page never exposed. #4 gains Accessibility.getFullAXTree, the real Chromium a11y tree, replacing the JS reimplementation the doc chose only to avoid the debugger permission. #19 gains real source-map parsing from disk. #21 gains direct access to the font FILE (opentype.js/fontkit on the real OS/2 tables) instead of estimating overrides from rendered advances. #22 gains full-page screenshots (Page.captureScreenshot captureBeyondViewport) and main-process overlay compositing, so the page is never modified to be numbered. #12 and #23 gain a real filesystem. And #5 gains genuinely TRUSTED synthetic events via CDP Input.dispatchMouseEvent — repairing the exact flaw the doc used to reject automated interaction in the first place.

THE AUDIT HARNESS IS THE MOST VALUABLE UNSHIPPED ARTIFACT IN THE PROJECT AND IT IS NOT IN THE SOURCE TREE. Session-Notes.md documents scratchpad/audit.js + audit-lib.js + why.js + why-inject.js + build-audit.js + resolve-deps.js: a tool that EXTRACTS the real functions out of content.js (resolving their dependencies automatically), runs them in Chrome over CDP, builds each component's preview, and compares it against the live element on three fingerprints. It found and fixed four real product bugs. Its measured trajectory: PASS 111 -> 114 -> 120 of 144; MOTION-DIFF 1 -> 0; PAINT-DIFF 11 -> 8 -> 1. In Electron this harness stops being scaffolding and becomes product code, because webContents.debugger is the same protocol. Ask for the scratchpad directory before designing #7 or #8.

THE AUDIT HARNESS'S OWN HARD-WON RULES, all from Session-Notes and all of which will bite anyone rebuilding it: (1) THE TOOL MUST VERIFY ITSELF BEFORE IT VERIFIES ANYTHING — the first run reported 144 defects and every single one was phantom, because the site's CSS had not loaded in headless Chrome; the fix was to wait for the stylesheet rule count to STABILISE (4 identical consecutive reads), run a health check before starting, and use a real user-agent. (2) Comparing an ANIMATING page against a fresh preview yields phantom differences; you must freeze with getAnimations().forEach(a => {a.currentTime=0; a.pause()}) on BOTH sides — and ONE freeze left 5 phantom diffs, so freeze TWICE (after 60ms, then again after 40ms). (3) AUDIT BLINDNESS: an early audit script selected .card elements directly instead of going through the real extraction pipeline, so it reported 120/144 passing while the user was looking at empty previews. Any audit MUST run the FULL pipeline (pass 1 + pass 2 + ranking), not hand-picked elements.

MEASURED NUMBERS WORTH CARRYING OVER (all from the code comments and Session-Notes, all real measurements on real sites): motion recording yields 6 of 80 components with exportable motion, while 77 of 80 carry real listener metadata — i.e. behaviour metadata is 13x more available than recordable motion. Component detection on kinetics.colorion.co went 7 -> 144 cards after the two-tier dedup fix, with MDN as a control growing 0.8%. Adding structure/classes to the dedup signature UNCONDITIONALLY inflates MDN by 62-74%; adding child count inflates it 61%; motion alone gives 0% — which is why the escalation is conditional on seeing 3 distinct motions in a group. Lazy-mount sweeping takes uiverse.io from 1 mounted component to 34. 12 of 94 keyframes in one motion library reference a CSS variable (the gap that made dots animate to transparent). 20 of ~1025 rules on kinetics (1.95%) and 8 of ~476 on MDN (1.68%) migrate from base to state rules under the widened ANY_STATE_RE, and every one was a genuine open-state. Revealing collapsed disclosures on MDN opened 111 <details> plus 9 aria-expanded and the page returned byte-identical. Nesting resolution handles 160 of 294 nested selectors on tailwindcss.com, which also has 2 real @starting-style blocks. Tailwind Docs 6082 rules -> 6082 after the nesting rebuild: zero inflation, zero duplication.

THE MOST COUNTER-INTUITIVE MEASURED RESULT IN THE ENTIRE PROJECT, because it contradicts the obvious design and was tested TWICE: aiming interactions at the inner controls of a component records LESS motion, not more. Replacing the component-centre aim with a trigger aim took recorded motion from 6 to 0; using it as a centre-first RETRY took it from 6 to 1, even with a 900-second budget that rules out starvation. The stated cause: every extra press leaves the page in a state the components recorded AFTERWARDS no longer animate from. The recorder therefore deliberately aims at exactly one point — the component's own centre — and accepts the coverage loss. Related and equally important: the '24 of 26 demos reached by hover+click' ground truth was measured on whole .card units, NOT on the exported component; much of that motion happens in SIBLINGS outside the pressed element's subtree (confetti particles appended elsewhere) and is therefore not expressible in an exported component at all. Any future coverage work must re-measure the ceiling on the EXPORTED unit first.

SILENT-FAILURE CATALOGUE — the doc's Strategic Theme #4 ('silent failures are the real enemy: any feature that does not know it has failed is a liability, not an asset') is backed by five concrete instances found in the shipped code, and each one is a trap for the port: (1) a dropped @property registration produces NO error and NO colour change, but the animation and the gradient quietly vanish because an unregistered custom property interpolates DISCRETELY; (2) a cross-origin stylesheet throws SecurityError on .cssRules and its rules are dropped with no signal at all; (3) a closed shadow root is simply invisible, so its components come back unstyled and stateless; (4) a font that fails to load shifts every text and invalidates every measurement while reporting success; (5) CSSNestedDeclarations rules (Chrome 130+) carry declarations with no selectorText, so any walker keying on selectorText drops them without a trace. Add a sixth from the ported environment: the extension's own preview iframe is ~150px wide, so mobile media queries fire inside it and the preview silently disagrees with the real page.

TWO REGEXES MUST STAY IN LOCKSTEP OR THE STATE MATRIX GETS WORSE THAN NOT HAVING IT: every marker ANY_STATE_RE recognises (content.js:4267-4275) must also be STRIPPABLE by baseSelector (content.js:4519-4544). If a marker is recognised but not stripped, the rule is filed as a state and then fails the very match test that filing it there was meant to let it pass — leaving it worse off than if it had stayed a resting rule. The code says this explicitly in a comment. Also tested and REJECTED, do not re-add: bare `.open`, bare `.active`, `.show`, `.selected` as state markers — half the web uses them for the current tab or the current nav link, and moving those rules out of the resting set leaves such elements previewing unstyled on every site. `.active` is called out as 'the one marker with real reach' and is excluded on purpose.

TESTED AND REJECTED, DO NOT REPEAT (from Session-Notes, each with measurements): guessing open-state classes by adding open/show/active onto ancestors — live measurement showed it failed to open 3 of 5 panels (one was behind a media query no class can open) and took credit for the 2 that were already open. Adding structure or class names unconditionally to the dedup signature (+62-74% on MDN). Adding descendant count to the discriminator key (+61% on MDN). Removing the viewport-area penalty from paintScore entirely — it is the only thing keeping <body> and page wrappers out of the list, from which they would swallow everything via the taken.contains rule; the exemption must stay conditional on repetition. Passing a sample element to ruleCssText inside componentStateRules — a state rule read from an element NOT in that state resolves to RESTING values and corrupts the export.

PLATFORM GOTCHAS THAT SURVIVE THE PORT: requestAnimationFrame NEVER fires in a hidden tab/window, so any wait built on rAF alone freezes forever — the recorder's whole pass 3 is skipped unless document.visibilityState === 'visible', and every rAF wait needs a setTimeout backstop. In Electron the equivalent hazard is a backgrounded/occluded BrowserWindow; set backgroundThrottling:false on any WebContents used for measurement. Also: `node --check` is NOT sufficient validation for regex-heavy code — the author shipped `/[أإآٱ]//g`, which parsed cleanly as a division by an undefined variable and only exploded at runtime. Run real tests after touching any regex, especially the Arabic ones. And use \p{L} rather than the Arabic Unicode block 0600-06FF for language splitting: the block contains the Arabic comma and the Arabic-Indic digits ٠-٩, which breaks matching and prevents duplicate merging.
